## Summary

The CITGM integration installs JSONStream's dependency tree without configuring the Git-dependency policy required by npm 12. Both Node 22 and Node 23 stop with `EALLOWGIT` while resolving a Git dependency. These are two occurrences of one fixture-policy mismatch.

## Affected run

Branch: `latest`, commit `c039090578a5b21a1aa3aba9c96e199feaf1823a`, npm `12.1.0`.

Workflow: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35779328486

* [Node 22: JSONStream@1.3.5](https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35779328486/job/106953426386)
* [Node 23: JSONStream@1.3.5](https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35779328486/job/106949098092)

The corresponding jobs in the [npm 11.20.0 release run](https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35787155620) passed.

## Failure

```text
npm error code EALLOWGIT
npm error Fetching packages of type "git" have been disabled
npm error Refusing to fetch "fomatto@git://github.com/BonsaiDen/Fomatto.git#468666f600b46f9067e3da7200fd9df428923ea6"
```

This occurs during:

```sh
npm install --no-audit --no-fund
```

The source archive has already been downloaded and extracted. Installation is blocked by policy before the package tests execute.

## Root cause

npm 12 intentionally changed `allow-git` and `allow-remote` to default to `none`, documented in the [npm 12.0.0 breaking changes](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/c039090578a5b21a1aa3aba9c96e199feaf1823a/CHANGELOG.md#1200-2026-07-08).

JSONStream's dependency tree requires the Git-hosted `fomatto` package, but the integration does not provide a fixture-specific opt-in or remove that legacy dependency requirement. npm is enforcing its configured policy.

The failure also occurs on supported Node 22. It must not be attributed to the separate unsupported Node 23 matrix entry.

## Proposed resolution

Review the intended fixture dependency tree and either eliminate the legacy Git dependency through a suitable fixture update or explicitly configure the minimum Git policy necessary for this trusted integration case. Preserve npm's production defaults and avoid blanket opt-ins across unrelated CITGM packages.

The npm/cli matrix generator consumes CITGM metadata, so the solution must identify whether the fixture metadata belongs upstream in CITGM or whether npm/cli needs integration-specific handling. Changes to generated npm/cli workflows must also update their templates.

## Acceptance criteria

* The intended JSONStream dependency tree installs on supported npm 12 runtimes and its tests actually execute.
* The same integration remains compatible with the v11 branch.
* The scope and rationale of any Git-dependency opt-in are explicit.
* Any subsequent failure is investigated on its own evidence rather than treating removal of `EALLOWGIT` as proof that the entire job is fixed.

## Scope boundary

This is independent of #10016, #10020, the Node 23 engine mismatch, and the native-build flag forwarding failure. Allowing Git dependencies does not make `--build-from-source` a valid npm 12 CLI flag.

### Current Behavior

Using Guix to to build `taler-util`, `npm install` crashes like the following:

Despite the `package.json` dependencies being patched to be absolute file names, which npm appears to be satisfied with, npm tries to reach to the network, fails (this happens in a containerized, isolated environment) and crashes without a useful error.

### Expected Behavior

A useful error should be produced instead of a crash asking me to file a bug.

### Steps To Reproduce

I'm using these components:
```
node@26.10.0 node-big-integer@1.6.52 node-esbuild@0.28.2 node-fflate@0.8.3 node-follow-redirects@1.16.0 node-hash-wasm@4.12.0 node-jed@1.1.1 node-tslib@2.8.1 node-types-follow-redirects@22.14.0
+ node-types-node@22.14.0 node-typescript@6.0.3
```

I was not able to reproduce outside of the minimal Guix build container; at least it should be easy to reproduce with GNU Guix, which can run on top of any GNU/Linux distribution (to install, see: https://guix.gnu.org/manual/devel/en/guix.html#Binary-Installation-1, and use the `guix-install.sh` script).
```
guix time-machine -q --url=https://codeberg.org/guixotic/guix -commit=npm-crash-issue-10030-repro -- build -K taler-util
```

## Situation

When [.github/workflows/create-node-pr.yml](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/.github/workflows/create-node-pr.yml) is executed to promote an npm release for packaging into Node.js, the following deprecation warnings are logged:

- a Node.js 20 deprecation warning from GitHub Actions and 
- a [DEP0040](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/deprecations.html#DEP0040) `node:punycode module` deprecation warning

## Logs

https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35881707767

> Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v3. For more information see: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/

https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35881707767/job/107251530925

```console
Run actions/checkout@v3
(node:2429) [DEP0040] DeprecationWarning: The `punycode` module is deprecated. Please use a userland alternative instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

## Suggestion

Update the template https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/c039090578a5b21a1aa3aba9c96e199feaf1823a/scripts/template-oss/create-node-pr-yml.hbs#L24 :

| FROM                                                               | TO                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [actions/checkout@v3](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v3) | [actions/checkout@v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v7) |

- [actions/checkout@v3](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v3) is an outdated release (originally from Mar 2022) which targets usage on `node16`. It is forced to run under `node24`.
- [actions/checkout@v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v7) is the current release which targets usage natively on `node24`

Although this is a simple update, I prefer to leave a PR to the npm team, since I'm not able to test PR creation from the [npm/cli](https://github.com/npm/cli) repo into the [nodejs/node](https://github.com/nodejs/node) end-to-end.

When [.github/workflows/create-node-pr.yml](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/.github/workflows/create-node-pr.yml) is executed to promote an npm release for packaging into Node.js, the following deprecation warnings are logged:

- a Node.js 20 deprecation warning from GitHub Actions and 
- a [DEP0040](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/deprecations.html#DEP0040) `node:punycode module` deprecation warning

## Logs

https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35881707767

> Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v3. For more information see: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/

https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/35881707767/job/107251530925

```console
Run actions/checkout@v3
(node:2429) [DEP0040] DeprecationWarning: The `punycode` module is deprecated. Please use a userland alternative instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

## Suggestion

Update the template https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/c039090578a5b21a1aa3aba9c96e199feaf1823a/scripts/template-oss/create-node-pr-yml.hbs#L24 :

| FROM                                                               | TO                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [actions/checkout@v3](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v3) | [actions/checkout@v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v7) |

- [actions/checkout@v3](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v3) is an outdated release (originally from Mar 2022) which targets usage on `node16`. It is forced to run under `node24`.
- [actions/checkout@v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/tree/v7) is the current release which targets usage natively on `node24`

Although this is a simple update, I prefer to leave a PR to the npm team, since I'm not able to test PR creation from the [npm/cli](https://github.com/npm/cli) repo into the [nodejs/node](https://github.com/nodejs/node) end-to-end.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues
- [ ] I believe this is a new issue

Related: #9835 (npm's own remediation prompt suggests the exact command that crashes), #6006 (same error message, different trigger)

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [X] I am using the latest npm

### Current Behavior

`npm install -g --allow-scripts=<pkg>` with **no positional package spec** always crashes with `Cannot destructure property 'name' of '.for' as it is undefined.` — including the exact command npm itself prints in the `install-scripts` remediation warning:

```
npm warn install-scripts Run `npm install -g --allow-scripts=ffmpeg-static` to allow these scripts once,
                 or `npm config set allow-scripts=ffmpeg-static --location=user` to allow them for all global installs.
```

This makes the documented one-off escape hatch for a blocked install script unusable, and the `npm config set --location=user` alternative is a permanent policy change for a one-time need.

```
npm error Cannot destructure property 'name' of '.for' as it is undefined.
npm error A complete log of this run can be found in: ~/.npm/_logs/...-debug-0.log
```

```
verbose stack TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of '.for' as it is undefined.
verbose stack     at [diffTrees] (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js:454:20)
verbose stack     at Arborist.reify (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js:138:29)
verbose stack     at async Install.exec (.../npm/lib/commands/install.js:176:5)
verbose stack     at async Npm.exec (.../npm/lib/npm.js:194:9)
```

### Expected Behavior

Either the install should succeed, or `install.js` should not feed a synthetic `.` spec into Arborist in this case. Failing with a `TypeError` is never acceptable.

### Steps To Reproduce

Deterministic, and not specific to any package:

```console
$ npm install -g --allow-scripts=left-pad
npm error Cannot destructure property 'name' of '.for' as it is undefined.

$ npm install -g --allow-scripts=left-pad left-pad     # works
added 1 package in 249ms
```

The same holds for the space-separated form (`--allow-scripts left-pad`), and for any package name.

### Root cause

`install.js` substitutes a `.` spec when a global install has no positional args, so that npm reifies the global tree:

```js
// npm/lib/commands/install.js:138
if (isGlobalInstall && !args.length) {
  args = ['.']
}
```

That spec is passed to Arborist as `add`, and ends up in `_resolvedAdd`. The global tree root has no dependency entry for it, so the `edgesOut` lookup misses and `undefined` is added to `#explicitRequests`:

```js
// @npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:651
for (const spec of this[_resolvedAdd]) {
  if (spec.tree === tree) {
    this.#explicitRequests.add(tree.edgesOut.get(spec.name))   // <-- undefined
  }
}
```

`diffTrees` then destructures it under the global branch:

```js
// @npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js:449
if (this.options.global && this.explicitRequests.size) {
  ...
  for (const { name } of this.explicitRequests) {   // <-- TypeError
```

Confirmed by instrumenting `Set.prototype.add` during the crash; the `undefined` originates at `build-ideal-tree.js:653`.

Passing a real spec masks the bug, because that spec does get an edge in `edgesOut` — which is also why the workaround below works.

### Suggested fix

Guard the lookup in `build-ideal-tree.js:651` (and the `globalExplicitUpdateNames` loop right below it, which has the same shape):

```js
for (const spec of this[_resolvedAdd]) {
  if (spec.tree === tree) {
    const edge = tree.edgesOut.get(spec.name)
    if (edge) {
      this.#explicitRequests.add(edge)
    }
  }
}
```

### Workaround

Repeat the package as a positional spec:

```console
npm install -g --allow-scripts=ffmpeg-static ffmpeg-static
```

Note that a project `.npmrc` `allow-scripts` is not consulted for global installs, so the `npm config set ... --location=user` route is the only other option, and it is global/permanent.

### Environment

* npm -v: 12.0.2
* node -v: v26.8.1
* OS: Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.7-arch1-1
* Prefix: asdf-installed nodejs 26.8.1

## Summary

The npm 12.2.0 release integration runs npm's smoke tests on Node.js nightly `v27.0.0-pre`. npm correctly emits its unsupported-engine warning, but the smoke test for `npm` with no arguments requires empty stderr and fails.

This is different from #10024. That issue owns the stale stable Node 23 target, while nightly is intentionally retained as forward-compatibility coverage.

## Affected run

Release: npm 12.2.0

Branch: `latest`

Commit: `c276cadf785c1018d82dd287fe7742567055efb9`

Workflow: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36746332014

Failing job: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36746332014/job/110043487985

## Failure

The smoke test invokes npm on Node.js nightly:

```text
npm info using npm@12.2.0
npm info using node@v27.0.0-pre
npm warn cli npm v12.2.0 does not support Node.js v27.0.0-pre.
```

The command exits as expected, but the test fails because stderr is not empty:

```text
not ok 2 - should have no stderr output
found: "npm warn cli npm v12.2.0 does not support Node.js v27.0.0-pre..."
wanted: ""
```

The workspace test failure is later obscured by the existing result-aggregation bug:

```text
exit: STEPEXIT: numeric argument required
```

That aggregation defect is already tracked as a cross-cutting item in #10027, but fixing it will only expose the original smoke-test failure more accurately.

## Investigation and resolution

Decide what the nightly integration contract should be when nightly is intentionally outside npm's declared engine range. Preserve nightly forward-compatibility coverage without suppressing engine warnings globally or weakening the supported-runtime assertions.

Possible resolutions must distinguish expected unsupported-engine output in the nightly integration context from unexpected stderr on supported runtimes.

## Acceptance criteria

* The nightly npm test job has an explicit contract for npm's unsupported-engine warning.
* Supported-runtime smoke assertions remain unchanged.
* The npm test suite actually executes on nightly and reports its real result.
* The workflow propagates the original numeric failure code rather than the literal `STEPEXIT` string.

## Scope boundary

This is not the stable Node 23 matrix mismatch in #10024. It is also separate from the Node nightly source-download failure in #10016 and the native CITGM fixture failures.

## Summary

The npm 12.2.0 release integration fails to install both `leveldown@6.1.1` and `microtime@3.1.1` on Node.js nightly. Their older node-gyp versions do not use the workflow's current Node source-directory configuration and try to install headers for the prerelease runtime.

Both failures share one root cause and should remain in one issue.

## Affected run

Release: npm 12.2.0

Branch: `latest`

Commit: `c276cadf785c1018d82dd287fe7742567055efb9`

Workflow: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36746332014

Failing jobs:

* `leveldown@6.1.1`: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36746332014/job/110043492199
* `microtime@3.1.1`: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36746332014/job/110043492222

## Failure

The workflow exports:

```sh
npm_package_config_node_gyp_nodedir="${{ steps.install.outputs.nodedir }}"
```

Both fixtures then invoke `node-gyp-build`. Their bundled node-gyp versions try to install headers for the prerelease Node version instead of using the already-built Node source directory.

`leveldown` uses node-gyp 8.4.1:

```text
gyp info using node@27.0.0-pre | linux | x64
gyp ERR! stack Error: "pre" versions of node cannot be installed, use the --nodedir flag instead
```

`microtime` uses node-gyp 9.4.1 and fails with the same message.

## Root-cause status

Confirmed: both failures occur during native configure because node-gyp attempts its header-install path for a prerelease Node version.

Confirmed: the workflow already has a built Node directory and attempts to expose it through `npm_package_config_node_gyp_nodedir`.

Unresolved: whether the affected node-gyp versions require `npm_config_nodedir`, a direct `--nodedir` argument, fixture metadata, or another compatibility path in this npm 12 integration environment.

## Investigation and resolution

Verify how node-gyp 8.4.1 and 9.4.1 receive `nodedir` through npm lifecycle environments under npm 12. Use the minimum fixture-specific or workflow-level transport that makes the intended native build consume the existing Node source tree.

Confirm the fix with both fixtures because their node-gyp versions differ. Do not mark the issue fixed merely because installation reaches a later step.

## Acceptance criteria

* leveldown and microtime use the provided Node source directory on nightly.
* Neither fixture attempts to download or install headers for `v27.0.0-pre`.
* Both native builds complete and their package tests execute.
* Stable Node integration behavior remains unchanged.
* Any workflow change is also applied to its source template and assessed for `release/v11`.

## Scope boundary

This is separate from #10023. thread-sleep fails because CITGM passes the rejected npm CLI option `--build-from-source`; leveldown and microtime reach their native installer and fail while locating Node headers.

## Summary

The npm 11.21.0 Release workflow failed in `template-oss-release-please` after an HTTP request returned an nginx `502 Bad Gateway` response. The failure prevented GitHub tags and Releases from being created for the two packages changed by the release and skipped all downstream release-integration jobs.

Parent tracker: #10027

## Affected run

Release: npm 11.21.0

Branch: `release/v11`

Release commit: `e9f182ab8b45f7e2e87da4076e62376e99d7df54`

Workflow: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756679730

Failing job: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756679730/job/110028585934

The corresponding branch CI workflow passed: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756678607

## Missing GitHub release records

Both packages were successfully published to the npm registry, but the corresponding Git tags and GitHub Releases were not created:

| Package | Registry publication | Missing Git tag | Missing GitHub Release |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm@11.21.0` | Published | `v11.21.0` | `v11.21.0` |
| `@npmcli/config@10.14.0` | Published | `config-v10.14.0` | `config-v10.14.0` |

The previous records, `v11.20.0` and `config-v10.13.0`, exist normally.

## Root cause

The fatal error was an unhandled HTTP `502 Bad Gateway` response during the release-please step:

```text
Release Please failed
HttpError: <html>
<head><title>502 Bad Gateway</title></head>
...
```

release-please normally uses the GitHub API to discover releases, tags, release pull requests, commits, and changed-file lists and to create GitHub release records. The log does not include the request URL, so the exact GitHub API endpoint or intermediary that returned the 502 cannot be identified from this run.

The following messages were not the fatal cause:

* release-please reported 11 of 13 component releases because the two newly changed components did not yet have their new GitHub release records.
* The old commit `a3b5559a18f489999c09e4f94694e162a4e8e6f6` (`Fix typos in some files`) did not follow Conventional Commits syntax. release-please logged the parse warning and continued.

## Remediation

Re-run the complete failed workflow so that skipped dependent jobs are reevaluated:

```sh
gh run rerun 36756679730 --repo npm/cli
gh run watch 36756679730 --repo npm/cli
```

The workflow contains no npm publication step. A successful rerun should create both missing tags and GitHub Releases without republishing the already-published registry packages, then run downstream release integration.

If the 502 recurs, capture the request endpoint class, response status, and retry behavior before manually creating tags or releases. Do not create the tags first because that can change release-please's release detection.

## Acceptance criteria

* `v11.21.0` exists as a Git tag and GitHub Release.
* `config-v10.14.0` exists as a Git tag and GitHub Release.
* Both releases point to the intended npm 11.21.0 release commit and contain the generated release metadata.
* The Release workflow completes its release-please step.
* The skipped Release Integration jobs are executed and their results are recorded.
* A recurring HTTP failure includes enough diagnostics to identify the request and determine whether bounded retry handling is needed.

The npm 11.21.0 Release workflow failed in `template-oss-release-please` after an HTTP request returned an nginx `502 Bad Gateway` response. The failure prevented GitHub tags and Releases from being created for the two packages changed by the release and skipped all downstream release-integration jobs.

Parent tracker: #10027

## Affected run

Release: npm 11.21.0

Branch: `release/v11`

Release commit: `e9f182ab8b45f7e2e87da4076e62376e99d7df54`

Workflow: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756679730

Failing job: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756679730/job/110028585934

The corresponding branch CI workflow passed: https://github.com/npm/cli/actions/runs/36756678607

## Missing GitHub release records

Both packages were successfully published to the npm registry, but the corresponding Git tags and GitHub Releases were not created:

| Package | Registry publication | Missing Git tag | Missing GitHub Release |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm@11.21.0` | Published | `v11.21.0` | `v11.21.0` |
| `@npmcli/config@10.14.0` | Published | `config-v10.14.0` | `config-v10.14.0` |

The previous records, `v11.20.0` and `config-v10.13.0`, exist normally.

## Root cause

The fatal error was an unhandled HTTP `502 Bad Gateway` response during the release-please step:

```text
Release Please failed
HttpError: <html>
<head><title>502 Bad Gateway</title></head>
...
```

release-please normally uses the GitHub API to discover releases, tags, release pull requests, commits, and changed-file lists and to create GitHub release records. The log does not include the request URL, so the exact GitHub API endpoint or intermediary that returned the 502 cannot be identified from this run.

The following messages were not the fatal cause:

* release-please reported 11 of 13 component releases because the two newly changed components did not yet have their new GitHub release records.
* The old commit `a3b5559a18f489999c09e4f94694e162a4e8e6f6` (`Fix typos in some files`) did not follow Conventional Commits syntax. release-please logged the parse warning and continued.

## Remediation

Re-run the complete failed workflow so that skipped dependent jobs are reevaluated:

```sh
gh run rerun 36756679730 --repo npm/cli
gh run watch 36756679730 --repo npm/cli
```

The workflow contains no npm publication step. A successful rerun should create both missing tags and GitHub Releases without republishing the already-published registry packages, then run downstream release integration.

If the 502 recurs, capture the request endpoint class, response status, and retry behavior before manually creating tags or releases. Do not create the tags first because that can change release-please's release detection.

## Acceptance criteria

* `v11.21.0` exists as a Git tag and GitHub Release.
* `config-v10.14.0` exists as a Git tag and GitHub Release.
* Both releases point to the intended npm 11.21.0 release commit and contain the generated release metadata.
* The Release workflow completes its release-please step.
* The skipped Release Integration jobs are executed and their results are recorded.
* A recurring HTTP failure includes enough diagnostics to identify the request and determine whether bounded retry handling is needed.

body_text:
### Current Behavior

`npm view` / `npm ping` against a local HTTP registry stub (a plain `http.createServer` answering every request with 200) **never opens a TCP connection to the stub** and dies with `FETCH_ERROR` / `request-timeout` after the fetch timeout (~5s with `--fetch-timeout=5000`). With default flags the request just stalls (observed >30s). node's own clients against the same stub work instantly. The failure is identical on every box we tested — Linux and macOS.

### Expected Behavior

npm should connect to and fetch from the local registry stub, as node's own `http.request`/`fetch` do.

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained: start a stub in one node process, run `npm view` against it.

```js
// stub.mjs — answers any request with a minimal packument
import http from "node:http";
let hits = 0, conns = 0;
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  hits++;
  res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ _id: "left-pad", name: "left-pad", "dist-tags": { latest: "1.0.0" }, versions: { "1.0.0": { name: "left-pad", version: "1.0.0" } } }));
}).on("connection", () => conns++)
  .listen(0, "[redacted:ip]", () => console.log(`stub http://[redacted:ip]:${stub.address().port} — watch hits/conns here`));
```

```sh
npm view left-pad@^1.0.0 version --json --registry http://[redacted:ip]:<port> --fetch-retries=0 --fetch-timeout=5000
# -> ~5.2s, exit 1: npm error code FETCH_ERROR / "network timeout at: ..."
# stub-side: hits and TCP conns UNCHANGED — npm never connected
node -e 'fetch("http://[redacted:ip]:<port>/left-pad").then(r => console.log(r.status))'
# -> 200 in single-digit ms — node's own client is fine
npm ping --registry http://[redacted:ip]:<port> --fetch-retries=0 --fetch-timeout=5000
# -> same FETCH_ERROR, stub still never sees a socket
```

### Layer isolation (why we think it is make-fetch-happen, not npm wiring)

All of this in one session, npm 10.9.8 bundled tree:

1. **node `fetch` and `http.get`** against the stub: HTTP 200 in 3–25ms (stub sees the connection).
2. **npm CLI** (`view`, `ping`): `FETCH_ERROR` at ~5.2s with `--fetch-timeout=5000`; **stub-side TCP connection count and request bytes: 0**. `--loglevel=silly` shows `npm http fetch GET ... attempt 1 failed with FETCH_ERROR`, type `request-timeout`, stack inside `minipass-fetch/lib/index.js` timeout timer.
3. **make-fetch-happen@14.0.3 (npm's bundled copy) driven directly from a plain node script** — no npm, no npmrc, no config:
   ```js
   const mfh = makeRequire("<npm-install>/node_modules/make-fetch-happen/package.json")("make-fetch-happen");
   await mfh("http://[redacted:ip]:<port>/", { timeout: 5000 }); // -> FETCH_ERROR at 5006ms, stub saw 0 connections
   ```
   Identical hang. Instrumenting `http.request` inside that child: the options are well-formed enough (`hostname: "[redacted:ip]"`, `port`, `path: "/"`; note minipass-fetch's `getNodeRequestOptions` also sets `host: parsedURL.host` which contains `ip:port` — request.js:239-242 — but plain node handles that shape fine when hostname is present), the request fires `'socket'` with a socket that reports `remoteAddress`/`remotePort` as the stub and `connecting: false` — yet **the stub never receives the connection**. `'error'` never fires; the minipass-fetch `request-timeout` timer is what ends it.
4. **Plain node `http.request` with the exact same options shape** (including the `host: "ip:port"` quirk and an equivalent keepAlive agent + extras): HTTP 200 in 2–33ms every time. So the fault is not the options shape, not node's http stack, and not npm's CLI wiring — it is inside make-fetch-happen's agent/fetch layer.
5. Controls: real registry fine (`npm view left-pad@^999.0.0` → fast `E404` round-trip, 270–570ms); **closed** loopback port → fast `ECONNREFUSED` (216–355ms) — so npm's client does attempt connects and can see refusals; it is specifically the *listening local server* case that silently never connects.
6. Not a proxy/npmrc/env artifact: `npm config get proxy/https-proxy` → null; no `HTTP(S)_PROXY`/`npm_config_*` in env on the failing legs; `.npmrc` empty; `http://localhost:<port>` fails identically to `http://[redacted:ip]:<port>`.

### Environment

- npm 10.9.8 / node 22.23.1 / macOS arm64 (Darwin 27)
- npm 10.9.9 / node 22.23.3 / Linux x64 (GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, Linux 6.17)
- npm 10.9.8 / node 22.23.2 / macOS arm64 (GitHub-hosted macos-14, Darwin 23.6)
- Bundled layer: make-fetch-happen@14.0.3, minipass-fetch@4.0.1

All three boxes fail byte-for-byte identically, including the standalone make-fetch-happen repro on box 1.

### Why this matters

The "spin a stub registry and point npm at it" recipe is the standard way to make npm-behavior pins hermetic (E404 vs E5xx vs ECONNREFUSED classification, packument shapes). On current npm it silently cannot work on any of our Linux or macOS environments — the stub never sees a socket and the caller times out, which reads as a flake/hang rather than a clear error.

Happy to provide the full instrumented-child receipts or test candidate fixes.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

`npm publish --provenance` (also via `libnpmpublish`, e.g. through `lerna publish`) intermittently fails with:

```
TLOG_CREATE_ENTRY_ERROR error creating tlog entry - (409) an equivalent entry already exists in the transparency log with UUID <uuid>
```

The package is not published. In a monorepo release (lerna 10, `libnpmpublish@11.1.2`, npm 11.19.0, GitHub Actions) this left 22 of 23 packages published and one missing, so the release ended up half-done.

This looks like a retry-after-success path: Rekor commits the create-entry request, the client then times out or gets a retryable response and retries, and Rekor correctly answers 409 for the now-existing equivalent entry. The 409 is treated as fatal.

`@sigstore/sign` already has a recovery path for this (`TLogClient` fetches the existing entry when `fetchOnConflict` is true), but it's off:

- `sigstore` hard-codes `fetchOnConflict: false` in `initWitnesses` (`dist/config.js`) and doesn't read it from the options passed to `sigstore.attest()`.
- `libnpmpublish/lib/provenance.js` calls `sigstore.attest(...)`, so there is no way to enable it from npm today.

### Expected Behavior

A 409 for an equivalent existing Rekor entry should be recovered by fetching that entry and continuing, so that `npm publish --provenance` is idempotent with respect to tlog creation.

### Steps To Reproduce

Not deterministic (needs Rekor to commit an entry and the client to retry). Seen in CI on `npm publish --provenance` / `lerna publish` in a GitHub Actions workflow with `id-token: write`.

### Environment

- npm: 11.19.0
- libnpmpublish: 11.1.2 (via lerna 10.0.1)
- sigstore / @sigstore/sign: 4.1.1
- Node: LTS on `ubuntu-latest` (GitHub Actions)

### Additional context

Same root cause is tracked on the sigstore side in sigstore/sigstore-js#1708. There the maintainer prefers not to change the library default before a major release and suggested enabling it from the npm CLI instead. Since `sigstore` doesn't currently accept the option, a non-breaking fix would be:

1. `sigstore-js`: allow `fetchOnConflict` to be passed through `sigstore.attest()` options (default unchanged).
2. `libnpmpublish`: pass `fetchOnConflict: true` when generating provenance.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

Take a root whose `workspaces` lists a folder and a workspace inside that folder, `["packages/outer", "packages/outer/src/*"]`. With `install-strategy=linked`, npm installs nothing for the inner workspace. `packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules` is never created, so the inner workspace cannot resolve its own dependencies, and `npm install` reports `up to date` without fetching them. `npm ls --all` reports the workspace as `UNMET DEPENDENCY` / `missing: inner@file:…, required by root@1.0.0` and exits 1, and `npm ls --workspaces` leaves it out.

`npm ci` from a lockfile generated with `--install-strategy=hoisted` (which records the inner workspace's dependencies) gives the same result. With `install-strategy=hoisted`, everything works.

Related, but not the same:

- #9618 and #9090 (both closed) are about workspaces that sit side by side, not one inside another.
- #4774 is about a workspace that declares workspaces of its own, installed from inside it. Here the root declares both paths.

### Expected Behavior

The inner workspace's dependencies are installed and resolvable from it, and `npm ls` lists the workspace like any other, matching `install-strategy=hoisted`.

### Steps To Reproduce

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p packages/outer/src/inner
echo '{"name":"root","version":"1.0.0","workspaces":["packages/outer","packages/outer/src/*"]}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"outer","version":"1.0.0"}' > packages/outer/package.json
echo '{"name":"inner","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"is-number":"7.0.0"}}' > packages/outer/src/inner/package.json
echo 'install-strategy=linked' > .npmrc
npm install --no-audit --no-fund
# up to date in 128ms

ls packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules
# ls: cannot access 'packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules': No such file or directory

(cd packages/outer/src/inner && node -e "require.resolve('is-number')")
# Error: Cannot find module 'is-number'

npm ls --all
# root@1.0.0 <dir>
# ├── UNMET DEPENDENCY inner@file:<dir>/packages/outer/src/inner
# └── outer@1.0.0 -> ./packages/outer
# npm error code ELSPROBLEMS
# npm error missing: inner@file:<dir>/packages/outer/src/inner, required by root@1.0.0
```

With `install-strategy=hoisted` in `.npmrc` instead, `is-number` resolves from the inner workspace, and `npm ls --all` prints `inner@1.0.0 -> ./packages/outer/src/inner` and exits 0.

### Environment

- npm: 12.2.0 (also reproduced on 11.19.0)
- Node.js: v24.21.0
- OS Name: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- System Model Name: not hardware-specific
- npm config:

```ini
; "project" config from <dir>/.npmrc

install-strategy = "linked"
```

### Current Behavior

Take a root whose `workspaces` lists a folder and a workspace inside that folder, `["packages/outer", "packages/outer/src/*"]`. With `install-strategy=linked`, npm installs nothing for the inner workspace. `packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules` is never created, so the inner workspace cannot resolve its own dependencies, and `npm install` reports `up to date` without fetching them. `npm ls --all` reports the workspace as `UNMET DEPENDENCY` / `missing: inner@file:…, required by root@1.0.0` and exits 1, and `npm ls --workspaces` leaves it out.

`npm ci` from a lockfile generated with `--install-strategy=hoisted` (which records the inner workspace's dependencies) gives the same result. With `install-strategy=hoisted`, everything works.

Related, but not the same:

- #9618 and #9090 (both closed) are about workspaces that sit side by side, not one inside another.
- #4774 is about a workspace that declares workspaces of its own, installed from inside it. Here the root declares both paths.

### Expected Behavior

The inner workspace's dependencies are installed and resolvable from it, and `npm ls` lists the workspace like any other, matching `install-strategy=hoisted`.

### Steps To Reproduce

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p packages/outer/src/inner
echo '{"name":"root","version":"1.0.0","workspaces":["packages/outer","packages/outer/src/*"]}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"outer","version":"1.0.0"}' > packages/outer/package.json
echo '{"name":"inner","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"is-number":"7.0.0"}}' > packages/outer/src/inner/package.json
echo 'install-strategy=linked' > .npmrc
npm install --no-audit --no-fund
# up to date in 128ms

ls packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules
# ls: cannot access 'packages/outer/src/inner/node_modules': No such file or directory

(cd packages/outer/src/inner && node -e "require.resolve('is-number')")
# Error: Cannot find module 'is-number'

npm ls --all
# root@1.0.0 <dir>
# ├── UNMET DEPENDENCY inner@file:<dir>/packages/outer/src/inner
# └── outer@1.0.0 -> ./packages/outer
# npm error code ELSPROBLEMS
# npm error missing: inner@file:<dir>/packages/outer/src/inner, required by root@1.0.0
```

With `install-strategy=hoisted` in `.npmrc` instead, `is-number` resolves from the inner workspace, and `npm ls --all` prints `inner@1.0.0 -> ./packages/outer/src/inner` and exits 0.

- Node.js: v24.21.0
- OS Name: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- System Model Name: not hardware-specific
- npm config:

```ini
; "project" config from <dir>/.npmrc

install-strategy = "linked"
```

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [X] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [X] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

When a package is added or updated against an existing lockfile, and one of its new dependencies has an optional peer that conflicts with a version already hoisted at the root, npm writes a lockfile with an invalid peerOptional edge.

During placement npm does the right thing: it nests the dependency together with a copy of the optional peer that satisfies the range. Then `#fixDepFlags` prunes that copy. `calcDepFlags` keeps nodes reachable only through a peerOptional edge extraneous, and `#idealTreePrune` runs because the tree was loaded from a lockfile and mutated. Afterwards the nested dependency resolves the optional peer to the hoisted version, which does not satisfy it.

Real example: `jsdom@30` pulls in `@exodus/bytes`, which has an optional peer `@noble/hashes@"^1.8.0 || ^2.0.0"`, while `selfsigned` (via `pkijs@3.4.0`) needs `@noble/hashes@1.4.0` exactly. The silly log shows `placeDep node_modules/jsdom @noble/hashes@2.3.0 OK for: @exodus/bytes@1.15.1`, but that copy is gone from the saved lockfile:

- `npm ls` reports `@noble/hashes@1.4.0 invalid: "^1.8.0 || ^2.0.0" from node_modules/jsdom/node_modules/@exodus/bytes` (6 invalid edges).
- `npm ci` with the same npm accepts the lockfile (it trusts invalid peerOptional edges since #8981).
- npm 10 `npm ci` rejects it with `Missing: @noble/hashes@2.4.0 from lock file`.

A fresh install of the same `package.json` without a lockfile skips the prune and ends up valid. #4859 (fixed in 11.10.1) covered the fresh-install path only. #9249 comes from the same prune of extraneous optional peers; there the edge ends up missing, here it ends up pointing at a version that does not satisfy it.

### Expected Behavior

The nested copy of the optional peer stays, so the lockfile is valid and `npm ls` reports nothing invalid.

### Steps To Reproduce

`--before` pins `pkijs` to 3.4.0, which has the exact `@noble/hashes@1.4.0` dependency:

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"r","private":true,"devDependencies":{"jsdom":"26.1.0","selfsigned":"5.5.0"}}' > package.json
O="--package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts --before=2026-08-15"
npm install $O
npm install $O --save-exact jsdom@30.0.1
npm ls --package-lock-only @noble/hashes      # invalid edges, ELSPROBLEMS
npm ci --ignore-scripts                        # passes
rm -rf node_modules && npx -y npm@10 ci --ignore-scripts   # Missing: @noble/hashes@2.4.0 from lock file
```

- OS Name: macOS 26.5
- System Model Name: MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon)

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

Related but distinct: #8710 fixed overlapping `stat` calls by changing the lock maintenance loop from `setInterval` to `setTimeout`. The current implementation contains that fix; this report is an inode-identity failure.

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

Reproduced with npm 12.2.0 immediately before filing.

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

On Docker Desktop for macOS, `npx` fails with `ECOMPROMISED: Lock compromised` when npm's cache is a host bind served through virtiofs. Packages whose installation finishes before the first lock check usually pass; a larger installation fails reliably.

`libnpmexec/lib/with-lock.js` records the lock directory's inode and rejects the lock if a later `stat` returns a different inode. A preload tracing `fs.promises.stat`, `utimes`, `mkdir`, and `rmdir` around the lock captured:

```text
...313275 mkdir ok
...313275 stat  ok ino=2548552 mtimeMs=1791392313276.2095
...314275 stat  ok ino=2548554 mtimeMs=1791392313276.2095
```

There was no intervening `mkdir` or `rmdir`: the same directory returned a new inode with the same mtime while npm's reify workload was writing the package tree beside it. `with-lock.js` interprets the inode change as compromise and aborts.

Moving only `<cache>/_npx` to a container-local tmpfs makes the same command pass while the reusable `_cacache` remains on the virtiofs bind. The downstream investigation and workaround are tracked at https://github.com/filippolmt/toolbox/issues/1167.

### Expected Behavior

`npm exec` should not report a compromised lock merely because a remote/FUSE filesystem returns unstable inode identity for an unchanged lock directory. This is especially surprising because `with-lock.js` documents that the lock works across machines via NFS.

I am not proposing that inode checks simply be removed; the lock needs a compromise check whose assumptions hold on the remote filesystems it intends to support.

### Steps To Reproduce

On macOS with Docker Desktop using virtiofs file sharing:

```sh
cache=$(mktemp -d)
docker run --rm \
  -v "$cache:/home/toolbox/.npm" \
  --entrypoint sh ghcr.io/filippolmt/toolbox:latest \
  -lc 'npm install -g npm@latest >/dev/null && /home/toolbox/.npm-global/bin/npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.9.0 --help'
```

The command fails with `ECOMPROMISED`. The equivalent invocation succeeds when `_npx` is overlaid with local storage:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  -v "$cache:/home/toolbox/.npm" \
  --tmpfs /home/toolbox/.npm/_npx:rw,exec,uid=1000,gid=1000,mode=0700 \
  --entrypoint sh ghcr.io/filippolmt/toolbox:latest \
  -lc 'npm install -g npm@latest >/dev/null && /home/toolbox/.npm-global/bin/npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.9.0 --help'
```

A small isolated call to the same `withLock` with a delayed callback did not reproduce it; the inode change appears tied to the real reify workload.

### Environment

- npm: 12.2.0
- Node.js: v24.21.0
- OS Name: macOS host, Debian container under Docker Desktop
- System Model Name: Apple Silicon Mac
- npm cache filesystem: `virtiofs0 on /home/toolbox/.npm`, reported as `fuseblk` by `stat -f -c %T`
- control filesystem: container overlayfs

# Is there an existing issue for this?

Related, not the same: #4924 and #7015 report a version-specific unpublish that removed every version, but with `--force`. Here `--force` was not given, and the "Refusing to delete the last version" check did not stop it.

# This issue exists in the latest npm version

Reproduced on npm 11.19.0 and on `latest` of this repository (83ea1a1).

# Current Behavior

A package of mine (name left out here) had three versions: `0.0.0-stage`, `0.0.1`, and `0.1.0`. `0.1.0` was published about six minutes earlier, through a trusted publisher. Then:

```
npm unpublish <pkg>@0.0.1
```

printed `- <pkg>@0.0.1` and exited 0, but the registry removed the whole package: all three versions. The debug log shows a whole-package `DELETE`, and no `PUT`:

```
16 http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>?write=true 395ms (cache miss)
17 http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>?write=true 194ms (cache miss)
18 http fetch DELETE 401 https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>/-rev/3-56bf641ba8f19a0f2c2bd1d5197c6040 221ms
...
25 http fetch DELETE 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>/-rev/3-56bf641ba8f19a0f2c2bd1d5197c6040 814ms
30 verbose exit 0
```

(The 401 is the web login; the retry after it is the same request.)

The package can now not be published for 24 hours, and the three version numbers can never be used again.

The cause in the code:

- `lib/commands/unpublish.js` refuses when `versions.length === 1 && spec.rawSpec === versions[0]`. It reads `versions` with `pacote.packument()`, which requests the abbreviated packument (`Accept: application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json`).
- `libnpmpublish`'s `unpublish()` reads the full packument (`Accept: */*`) and deletes the whole package when that document has one version or none.

The check and the deletion read two different documents. When the full one lists fewer versions than the abbreviated one, the check passes and the deletion removes the whole package. body_text:
The discussion about the [removal of `npm-shrinkwrap`](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8938) mentions a few times allowing `overrides` to apply when `bundleDependencies` is used, with what looks like some agreement that it’d be useful. 

<details><summary>Quotes from the discussion</summary>

> The real issue to solve here, and one which I think is worth exploring, is allowing for overrides to take place even in a bundled/shrinkwrap setting. The discussion would be one of priority, I think. 
> https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8938#issuecomment-3862766889  
 
> ... I think the goal should be: 
> 1. Have a standard way that npm itself uses for it’s CLI to deliver an optimized CLI package for use primarily via npx 
> 2. Have a standard way for package authors to ship opinions on the shape of their dependencies that consumers can take control of via overrides 
> 3. Allow for package authors to specify dependencies included in the package source but not via npm managed tooling 
> https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8938#issuecomment-3873277646 

> I think those goals are on the money, and that right now we have 1. and 3. but not 2. due to overrides not having the highest priority 
> https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8938#issuecomment-3873406454 

</details>

We’re raising this issue to discuss whether you’d consider implementing it in `npm`. 

This is something that’d be helpful for our [GOV.UK Prototype Kit project](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-prototype-kit/). Our package is used: 

1. As a CLI run with `npx` that lets users easily create new prototypes
2. As a dependency of the created prototypes, where it provides the server for the prototype 

Our main audience is designers/user researchers that cannot be expected to know the ins and out of dependency management and software vulnerability. To take on the dependency management for them, we've [set up `bundleDependencies` to control which dependencies get installed](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-prototype-kit/pull/2584). Previously we used shrinkwrap to that same effect.

However, this prevents teams with more developer support from taking more control over the prototypes’ dependencies, leaving them unable to address vulnerabilities as quickly as their organisations expect to meet their security policies. 

This is where having `overrides` apply to bundled dependencies would be great! We could still abstract dependency management for less tech-savy users while giving control to teams that need quicker vulnerability resolutions.

1. As a CLI run with `npx` that lets users easily create new prototypes
2. As a dependency of the created prototypes, where it provides the server for the prototype 

Our main audience is designers/user researchers that cannot be expected to know the ins and out of dependency management and software vulnerability. To take on the dependency management for them, we've [set up `bundleDependencies` to control which dependencies get installed](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-prototype-kit/pull/2584). However, this prevents teams with more developer support from taking more control over the prototypes’ dependencies, leaving them unable to address vulnerabilities as quickly as their organisations expect to meet their security policies. 

This is where having `overrides` apply to bundled dependencies would be great! ### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

When npm cannot use the hidden lockfile (`node_modules/.package-lock.json`), arborist reads every `package.json` under `node_modules` to build the actual tree. In `lib/arborist/load-actual.js`, `#loadFSChildren` fans those reads out with `Promise.all`. `fs/promises.readFile` holds a file descriptor from `open()` until the read completes, so a folder with N packages holds N descriptors at once. Above the process fd limit the remaining reads fail with `EMFILE`.

`#loadFSNode` catches any read error and "soldiers on", creating the node with the error attached and no `version`. `diff.js` then sees `ideal.version !== actual.version` and marks the node `CHANGE`, so `npm install` removes and re-extracts packages that were already correct. At the default log level the only output is `changed N packages`, which is wrong; the real cause is only visible at `--loglevel silly`.

Driving arborist directly on such a tree:

```js
const Arborist = require('@npmcli/arborist')
const arb = new Arborist({ path: process.cwd() })
const actual = await arb.loadActual()
const codes = {}
for (const n of actual.inventory.values()) {
  for (const e of n.errors || []) codes[e.code] = (codes[e.code] || 0) + 1
}
console.log(codes) // { EMFILE: 293 } under ulimit -n 128 with 400 packages
```

Consequences beyond wasted time: the re-extracted packages re-run their install scripts; under `--offline` with a cold cache the install fails on a tree that was already correct; which packages are affected depends on the fd limit and directory order, so the same lockfile behaves differently on different hosts.

### Expected Behavior

A tree whose contents match the lockfile is reported as `up to date` regardless of the process fd limit. The number of simultaneously open `package.json` files should be bounded, as #7631 did for the cache index.


### Steps To Reproduce

```sh
docker run --rm -it --ulimit nofile=1024:1024 node:24 bash
# inside: any project with more than ~1000 packages in its lockfile
npm ci
touch node_modules                       # anything newer than .package-lock.json invalidates it
npm install --loglevel verbose
# → "shrinkwrap failed to load node_modules/.package-lock.json out of date, updated: node_modules"
# → "changed N packages"
```

Without the `--ulimit`, the same commands print `up to date`.


### Environment

- npm: 12.2.0 (also 11.19.0)
- Node.js: 24.21.0
- OS: Linux (any host or container with the default 1024 fd soft limit)
- Current npm configuration: default

# [BUG] `npm ci` accepts a lockfile that violates `overrides` when a hoisted package is reached through multiple override scopes

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### Current Behavior

When the same hoisted package is reached both through a global override and through a path-scoped override, npm 11's `npm ci` accepts a lockfile that does not satisfy those overrides. It installs the non-overridden version without an error, and `npm ls` does not report the tree as invalid.

In the reproduction below, both overrides require `brace-expansion@^5.0.12` under `minimatch`. The lockfile has `brace-expansion@5.0.9` there. npm 11 installs 5.0.9:

```
$ npx npm@11 ci
added 25 packages, and audited 26 packages in 406ms

$ npm ls brace-expansion
npm-override-repro@1.0.0
└─┬ tshy@4.1.3
  └─┬ minimatch@10.2.6
    └── brace-expansion@5.0.9
```

npm 10 rejects the same `package.json` and lockfile:

```
$ npx npm@10 ci
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync. Please update your lock file with `npm install` before continuing.
npm error
npm error Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12
```

Running `npm install` or `npm install --package-lock-only` with npm 11 doesn't repair the lockfile either; it treats the lockfile as already in sync. Regenerating with npm 10 does fix it.

Since overrides are commonly used to force patched versions of transitive dependencies, this is quite significant for security. Here the override silently has no effect, and `npm ci` doesn't catch it. This looks like a regression compared to npm 10.

### Expected Behavior

`npm ci` should fail with `Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12`, as npm 10 does. `npm install` should update the lockfile so the override is satisfied.

### Steps To Reproduce

Run this script. It creates a temporary project, generates a lockfile while the overrides pin `5.0.9`, then tightens the overrides to `^5.0.12` without updating the lockfile:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
dir=$(mktemp -d); cd "$dir"

write_pkg() {
  cat > package.json <<JSON
{
  "name": "npm-override-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": { "tshy": "4.1.3" },
  "overrides": {
    "minimatch": { "brace-expansion": "$1" },
    "tshy": { "sync-content": { "glob": { "minimatch": { "brace-expansion": "$1" } } } }
  }
}
JSON
}

# 1. Generate a lockfile while the overrides pin brace-expansion@5.0.9.
write_pkg "5.0.9"
npx -y npm@11 install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --silent

# 2. Tighten the overrides to ^5.0.12 without updating the lockfile.
write_pkg "^5.0.12"

for v in 10 11; do
  rm -rf node_modules
  echo "=== npm@$v ci"
  npx -y npm@$v ci --ignore-scripts 2>&1 | grep -E 'Invalid|Missing|added' || true
done
echo "=== installed tree (after npm@11 ci)"
npm ls brace-expansion || true
```

Output:

```
=== npm@10 ci
npm error Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12
=== npm@11 ci
added 25 packages, and audited 26 packages in 406ms
=== installed tree (after npm@11 ci)
npm-override-repro@1.0.0
└─┬ tshy@4.1.3
  └─┬ minimatch@10.2.6
    └── brace-expansion@5.0.9
```

The relevant structure is that `tshy` depends on `sync-content`, which depends on `glob@13`, which depends on `minimatch@^10`. That `minimatch` is hoisted to `node_modules/minimatch` and uses the hoisted `node_modules/brace-expansion@5.0.9`. So the same `minimatch` node is reached through both override scopes.

We hit this in a real project after an automated dependency update tool, which uses npm 11, generated overrides like these. The resulting lockfile passed locally with npm 11 but failed in CI on Node 18/20/22, which ships with npm 10.

### Environment

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### Current Behavior

When the same hoisted package is reached both through a global override and through a path-scoped override, npm 11's `npm ci` accepts a lockfile that does not satisfy those overrides. It installs the non-overridden version without an error, and `npm ls` does not report the tree as invalid.

In the reproduction below, both overrides require `brace-expansion@^5.0.12` under `minimatch`. The lockfile has `brace-expansion@5.0.9` there. npm 11 installs 5.0.9:

```
$ npx npm@11 ci
added 25 packages, and audited 26 packages in 406ms

$ npm ls brace-expansion
npm-override-repro@1.0.0
└─┬ tshy@4.1.3
  └─┬ minimatch@10.2.6
    └── brace-expansion@5.0.9
```

npm 10 rejects the same `package.json` and lockfile:

```
$ npx npm@10 ci
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync. Please update your lock file with `npm install` before continuing.
npm error
npm error Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12
```

Running `npm install` or `npm install --package-lock-only` with npm 11 doesn't repair the lockfile either; it treats the lockfile as already in sync. Regenerating with npm 10 does fix it.

Since overrides are commonly used to force patched versions of transitive dependencies, this is quite significant for security. Here the override silently has no effect, and `npm ci` doesn't catch it. This looks like a regression compared to npm 10.

### Expected Behavior

`npm ci` should fail with `Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12`, as npm 10 does. `npm install` should update the lockfile so the override is satisfied.

### Steps To Reproduce

Run this script. It creates a temporary project, generates a lockfile while the overrides pin `5.0.9`, then tightens the overrides to `^5.0.12` without updating the lockfile:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
dir=$(mktemp -d); cd "$dir"

write_pkg() {
  cat > package.json <<JSON
{
  "name": "npm-override-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": { "tshy": "4.1.3" },
  "overrides": {
    "minimatch": { "brace-expansion": "$1" },
    "tshy": { "sync-content": { "glob": { "minimatch": { "brace-expansion": "$1" } } } }
  }
}
JSON
}

# 1. Generate a lockfile while the overrides pin brace-expansion@5.0.9.
write_pkg "5.0.9"
npx -y npm@11 install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --silent

# 2. Tighten the overrides to ^5.0.12 without updating the lockfile.
write_pkg "^5.0.12"

for v in 10 11; do
  rm -rf node_modules
  echo "=== npm@$v ci"
  npx -y npm@$v ci --ignore-scripts 2>&1 | grep -E 'Invalid|Missing|added' || true
done
echo "=== installed tree (after npm@11 ci)"
npm ls brace-expansion || true
```

Output:

```
=== npm@10 ci
npm error Invalid: lock file's brace-expansion@5.0.9 does not satisfy brace-expansion@5.0.12
=== npm@11 ci
added 25 packages, and audited 26 packages in 406ms
=== installed tree (after npm@11 ci)
npm-override-repro@1.0.0
└─┬ tshy@4.1.3
  └─┬ minimatch@10.2.6
    └── brace-expansion@5.0.9
```

The relevant structure is that `tshy` depends on `sync-content`, which depends on `glob@13`, which depends on `minimatch@^10`. That `minimatch` is hoisted to `node_modules/minimatch` and uses the hoisted `node_modules/brace-expansion@5.0.9`. So the same `minimatch` node is reached through both override scopes.

We hit this in a real project after an automated dependency update tool, which uses npm 11, generated overrides like these. The resulting lockfile passed locally with npm 11 but failed in CI on Node 18/20/22, which ships with npm 10.

- Node.js: v24.18.0
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0); the same npm 10 failure also occurs on GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

On Windows, npm 12.2.0 does not recognise the sh shims that it writes itself. When an install has to inspect an existing shim, the bin check fails with EEXIST, although the shim points into the very package being installed:

```
npm error code EEXIST
npm error path <prefix>\prettier
npm error EEXIST: file already exists
npm error File exists: <prefix>\prettier
npm error Remove the existing file and try again, or run npm
npm error with --force to overwrite files recklessly.
```

Cause: the bin-links bundled in npm 12.2.0 carries two nested dependencies that disagree.

- `node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/cmd-shim` 9.0.2 writes the exec line of the sh shim as
  `exec "$PROG_EXE"  "$basedir_win/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs" "$@"`.
- `node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/read-cmd-shim` 7.0.0 matches sh shims with
  `/"[$]basedir[/]([^"]+?)"\s+"[$]@"/`, so it rejects every shim that cmd-shim 9 writes with `ENOTASHIM`.

`lib/check-bin.js` turns any read error other than `ENOENT` into EEXIST (`handleReadCmdShimError`), so npm treats its own shim as a foreign file.

A normal update is not affected: arborist moves the installed version and its bin paths aside (`[_retireShallowNodes]`) before `[_reifyNode]` calls `[_checkBins]`. The error appears when an existing shim is not moved aside first. The case that hit me: a global install was interrupted, the package folder was gone but its shims remained, and the reinstall failed. The only way out npm offers is `--force`.

read-cmd-shim 7.0.1 (npm/read-cmd-shim#137, merged 2026-09-23) already accepts `"$basedir(?:_win)?/"`, but npm 12.2.0 still bundles 7.0.0, and so does the 12.2.1 tarball (`next-12`).

### Expected Behavior

npm recognises its own shims and reinstalls the package, as it does for shims in the old `"$basedir/"` form.

### Steps To Reproduce

Fresh prefix, empty user config (`npm_config_userconfig` pointing to an empty file), npm 12.2.0, Node 24.20.0:

1. `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> prettier@3.3.3`. This writes `<prefix>\prettier`, `prettier.cmd` and `prettier.ps1`; the sh shim uses `$basedir_win`.
2. Delete `<prefix>\node_modules\prettier` and keep the three shims (what an interrupted install leaves behind).
3. `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> prettier@3.3.3` fails with the EEXIST error above.

Controls, each in its own fresh prefix:

- The same steps, but rewrite the exec line of the sh shim to the old `"$basedir/node_modules/..."` form before step 3: the install succeeds.
- The same steps with `--force` in step 3: the install succeeds.
- A normal update with the shims in place (`prettier@3.3.2`, then `prettier@3.3.3`): succeeds.

Direct check on the shim from step 1:

```js
require('<npm>/node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/read-cmd-shim')('<prefix>/prettier')
// read-cmd-shim 7.0.0 (bundled in npm 12.2.0 and 12.2.1): rejects with ENOTASHIM
// read-cmd-shim 7.0.1: resolves to 'node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs'
```

Suggested fix: bundle read-cmd-shim 7.0.1. bin-links 7.0.0 already allows it (`"read-cmd-shim": "^7.0.0"`).

### Environment

- npm: 12.2.0 (the 12.2.1 tarball on `next-12` bundles the same read-cmd-shim 7.0.0)
- Node.js: 24.20.0
- OS Name: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300
- System Model Name: not hardware-specific
- npm config:
```ini
; "env" config from environment
cache = "<sandbox>\\cache"
userconfig = "<sandbox>\\empty.npmrc"

; "cli" config from command line options
prefix = "<sandbox>\\prefix"

; node bin location = C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe
; node version = v24.20.0
; npm version = 12.2.0
```

```
npm error File exists: <prefix>\prettier
npm error Remove the existing file and try again, or run npm
npm error with --force to overwrite files recklessly.
```

Cause: the bin-links bundled in npm 12.2.0 carries two nested dependencies that disagree.

- `node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/cmd-shim` 9.0.2 writes the exec line of the sh shim as
  `exec "$PROG_EXE"  "$basedir_win/node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs" "$@"`.
- `node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/read-cmd-shim` 7.0.0 matches sh shims with
  `/"[$]basedir[/]([^"]+?)"\s+"[$]@"/`, so it rejects every shim that cmd-shim 9 writes with `ENOTASHIM`.

`lib/check-bin.js` turns any read error other than `ENOENT` into EEXIST (`handleReadCmdShimError`), so npm treats its own shim as a foreign file.

A normal update is not affected: arborist moves the installed version and its bin paths aside (`[_retireShallowNodes]`) before `[_reifyNode]` calls `[_checkBins]`. The error appears when an existing shim is not moved aside first. The case that hit me: a global install was interrupted, the package folder was gone but its shims remained, and the reinstall failed. The only way out npm offers is `--force`.

read-cmd-shim 7.0.1 (npm/read-cmd-shim#137, merged 2026-09-23) already accepts `"$basedir(?:_win)?/"`, but npm 12.2.0 still bundles 7.0.0, and so does the 12.2.1 tarball (`next-12`).

### Expected Behavior

npm recognises its own shims and reinstalls the package, as it does for shims in the old `"$basedir/"` form.

### Steps To Reproduce

Fresh prefix, empty user config (`npm_config_userconfig` pointing to an empty file), npm 12.2.0, Node 24.20.0:

1. `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> prettier@3.3.3`. This writes `<prefix>\prettier`, `prettier.cmd` and `prettier.ps1`; the sh shim uses `$basedir_win`.
2. Delete `<prefix>\node_modules\prettier` and keep the three shims (what an interrupted install leaves behind).
3. `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> prettier@3.3.3` fails with the EEXIST error above.

Controls, each in its own fresh prefix:

- The same steps, but rewrite the exec line of the sh shim to the old `"$basedir/node_modules/..."` form before step 3: the install succeeds.
- The same steps with `--force` in step 3: the install succeeds.
- A normal update with the shims in place (`prettier@3.3.2`, then `prettier@3.3.3`): succeeds.

Direct check on the shim from step 1:

```js
require('<npm>/node_modules/bin-links/node_modules/read-cmd-shim')('<prefix>/prettier')
// read-cmd-shim 7.0.0 (bundled in npm 12.2.0 and 12.2.1): rejects with ENOTASHIM
// read-cmd-shim 7.0.1: resolves to 'node_modules/prettier/bin/prettier.cjs'
```

Suggested fix: bundle read-cmd-shim 7.0.1. bin-links 7.0.0 already allows it (`"read-cmd-shim": "^7.0.0"`).

### Environment

- npm: 12.2.0 (the 12.2.1 tarball on `next-12` bundles the same read-cmd-shim 7.0.0)
- Node.js: 24.20.0
- OS Name: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300
- System Model Name: not hardware-specific
- npm config:
```ini
; "env" config from environment
cache = "<sandbox>\\cache"
userconfig = "<sandbox>\\empty.npmrc"

; "cli" config from command line options
prefix = "<sandbox>\\prefix"

; node bin location = C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe
; node version = v24.20.0
; npm version = 12.2.0
```

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

`npm install -g` of a package whose peer group resolves across multiple prerelease lines crashes with a `TypeError` from Arborist instead of installing (or reporting a peer conflict):

```
$ npm install -g --prefix /tmp/npm-repro @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.9.0
npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'children')
```

Verbose stack (npm 12.0.2 / @npmcli/arborist 10.0.2):

```
501 verbose stack TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'children')
501 verbose stack     at new PlaceDep (.../node_modules/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/arborist/lib/place-dep.js:306:32)
501 verbose stack     at #buildDepStep (.../node_modules/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1145:18)
501 verbose stack     at async Arborist.buildIdealTree (.../node_modules/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:188:7)
501 verbose stack     at async Arborist.reify (.../node_modules/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js:118:5)
501 verbose stack     at async Install.exec (.../node_modules/npm/node_modules/npm/lib/commands/install.js:176:5)
```

On npm 11.19.0 the same crash occurs at the same lines in arborist 9.x.

### Expected Behavior

No crash. If the peer set cannot be placed, npm should either complete the install (placing the conflicting peers deeper) or emit a proper `ERESOLVE` peer-conflict error with the usual `--force`/`--legacy-peer-deps` guidance.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use npm 11.19.0 or 12.0.2 (latest). No project needed; an empty global prefix is enough:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/npm-repro/lib/node_modules
   npm install -g --prefix /tmp/npm-repro @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.9.0
   ```
2. Observe the `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'children')` crash. Nothing gets installed.

Notes on the trigger: `@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui@0.9.0` declares 26 required `peerDependencies` with dual ranges such as `^0.1.0-rc.6 || ^0.1.1-rc.1`, while its regular dependencies pin `^0.1.0-rc.8` of the same packages and their dist-tags point at older lines (`latest` = `0.1.0-rc.6`, `next` = `0.1.1-rc.2`). Mixing those prerelease lines inside one peer set is what trips the bug. The previous release `0.8.6`, whose peers use single ranges (`^0.1.0-rc.7`), installs fine on the same npm versions, so the user-visible trigger is package shape, not user error.

### Environment

### Is there an existing issue for this?

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

Hi there! 

The `npm` tarball ships `package.json` with `workspaces` (`docs`, `smoke-tests`, `mock-globals`, `mock-registry`, `workspaces/*`), devDependencies on those private workspace packages, and a `dependencies` lifecycle script that runs `scripts/bundle-and-gitignore-deps.js`. None of those directories or scripts are in the tarball — `files` only ships `bin/`, `lib/`, `index.js`, `docs/content/`, `docs/output/`, and `man/`.

So every Arborist command run against the installed npm directory fails:

- `npm ls` reports the workspaces as `UNMET DEPENDENCY`
- `npm install --prefix <npm dir> <pkg>` fails with `E404 @npmcli/docs@^1.0.0`
- `npm i --package-lock-only` fails resolving the devDependencies (`EALLOWREMOTE` on the `tap` tarball URL)
- `npm audit` fails with `ENOLOCK`, and the lockfile cannot be created because of the above

`--omit=dev` does not change this, since omitted deps are still resolved per the docs.

### Expected Behavior

The published manifest should only reference what the tarball ships. Then `npm ls`, `npm install`, and `npm audit` work inside `$(npm root -g)/npm`, and a user can inspect or patch the bundled tree with npm itself.

`scripts/publish.js` already rewrites `package.json` at release time, so stripping `workspaces`, `devDependencies`, and the dev-only `scripts` entries there would fix it. Happy to send that PR if that direction is acceptable.

To be clear, this is not a request to bump any dependency. The request is that the published manifest only reference what the tarball contains.

### Steps To Reproduce

**1.** Install npm 12.0.2 into a scratch prefix:

```sh
npm install -g --prefix /tmp/npm-test npm@12.0.2
NPMDIR=/tmp/npm-test/lib/node_modules/npm
```

**2.** List the tree:

```sh
/tmp/npm-test/bin/npm ls --depth=0 --prefix "$NPMDIR"
```

```
+-- UNMET DEPENDENCY @npmcli/docs@^1.0.0
+-- UNMET DEPENDENCY @npmcli/mock-globals@^1.0.0
+-- UNMET DEPENDENCY @npmcli/mock-registry@^1.0.0
+-- UNMET DEPENDENCY @npmcli/template-oss@5.1.1
...
```

**3.** Install anything into that directory:

```sh
/tmp/npm-test/bin/npm install --prefix "$NPMDIR" --no-save ip-address@10.7.0
```

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@npmcli%2fdocs - Not found
npm error 404  The requested resource '@npmcli/docs@^1.0.0' could not be found or you do not have permission to access it.
```

**4.** Try to create a lockfile so `npm audit` can run:

```
/tmp/npm-test/bin/npm i --package-lock-only --prefix "$NPMDIR"
npm error code EALLOWREMOTE
npm error Fetching packages of type "remote" have been disabled
npm error Refusing to fetch "https://registry.npmjs.org/tap/-/tap-16.3.10.tgz"
```

**5.** Stub the four workspace directories with a `package.json` each and repeat step 3. The install then fails in the `dependencies` lifecycle script:

```
npm error command sh -c node scripts/bundle-and-gitignore-deps.js && node scripts/dependency-graph.js
npm error Error: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/npm/scripts/bundle-and-gitignore-deps.js'
```

```
  ; npm version = 12.0.2
  ; cwd = ~
  ; HOME = ~
```

## Summary

When both --diff operands are local package directories, npm diff packages those directories through libnpmdiff and pacote. Pacote runs each directory package's prepare lifecycle unless --ignore-scripts is set. A command that appears read-only can therefore modify files or perform other actions declared by the selected package before showing the diff.

I am reporting this as a command behavior/UX issue, not as a security or bounty vulnerability. The user must run npm in, or explicitly select, the local project content.

## Pre-submission checks

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a report covering this same `npm diff` and local `prepare`-script behavior.
- [x] I reproduced this with npm 12.0.2, the current latest release according to the npm registry at the time of this update.
- [x] This is not a request to update a dependency solely to address a CVE.
## Environment

- npm 12.0.2
- Node.js 26.5.0
- Windows
- Observed source revision: c9876d7ea7150b0702e4151210b9fa1a8dbc7fbf

## Safe reproduction

Create left/package.json:

    {
      "name": "prepare-repro",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "scripts": { "prepare": "node prepare.js" }
    }

Create left/prepare.js:

    require('node:fs').writeFileSync('prepare-ran.txt', 'ran\n')

Create left/index.js containing:

    module.exports = 'left'

Create right/package.json:

    { "name": "prepare-repro", "version": "1.0.1" }

Create right/index.js containing:

    module.exports = 'right'

From the temporary parent directory, run:

    npm diff --diff=./left --diff=./right

After completion, left/prepare-ran.txt exists and is included in the computed diff because prepare ran before the package file list was created.

Control case:

    npm diff --ignore-scripts --diff=./left --diff=./right

After removing the marker, the control command does not recreate it.

## Expected behavior

Preferably, npm diff should not execute lifecycle scripts by default because it is an inspection command. If generated build artifacts must be compared, an explicit opt-in could retain that behavior. At minimum, the documentation and terminal output should clearly warn that local and Git operands may execute prepare.

## Relevant flow

- lib/commands/diff.js:55-62 passes normal flat options to libnpmdiff.
- workspaces/libnpmdiff/lib/index.js:35-39 obtains tarballs for both manifests.
- pacote/lib/dir.js:33-59 runs prepare when present and not ignored.
- pacote/lib/dir.js:74-82 runs preparation before generating the package file list.

## Impact and limitations

- Inspection can have surprising side effects and can alter the package before the diff is calculated.
- Scripts run with the invoking user's permissions, as normal npm lifecycle scripts do.
- --ignore-scripts prevents the behavior.
- The demonstrated case requires user-selected local project content; I did not establish an eligible npm bug-bounty attack path.
- Pacote may intentionally run prepare to match package materialization semantics. If so, documentation and warning improvements may be preferable to changing the default.

## Suggested remediation

For npm diff, consider setting ignoreScripts: true when materializing directory operands unless the user explicitly opts in. Please retain a regression test for --ignore-scripts and verify ordinary registry comparisons remain unchanged.

---

I reviewed the resulting analysis, verified claims against the cited source code, and reproduced behaviors locally where stated. No report was submitted or external system modified autonomously by the AI.

### Current Behavior

`npm ls --omit=optional --all` continues to include optional dependencies in its output.

_However_, `npm ls --omit=dev --all` excludes all development-only dependencies.

_Additionally_, `npm i --omit=optional` excludes all optional dependencies from being installed ([docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json#optionaldependencies)).

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### This issue exists in the latest npm version

- [x] I am using the latest npm

### This is not just a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

- [x] This is not solely a request to bump a dependency for a CVE

### Current Behavior

Changing a Git dependency’s full commit SHA in `package.json`, then running `npm install`, leaves the old commit in both `package-lock.json` and `node_modules`. The command succeeds and reports that everything is up to date.

### Expected Behavior

`npm install` should detect that the requested commit differs from the locked commit, install the requested commit, and update `package-lock.json`.

### Steps To Reproduce

This example uses two sibling directories: `dependency` contains a Git package with two commits, and `consumer` installs that package. Run the commands in the same Bash session.

1. **Create the dependency and its two commits.**

   Both commits have the same package version but different file contents.

   ```bash
   mkdir git-dependency-update-test
   cd git-dependency-update-test
   mkdir dependency consumer

   cd dependency
   git init
   echo '{"name":"dependency","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json

   echo 'old content' > content.txt
   git add .
   git commit -m "Old content"
   old_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

   echo 'new content' > content.txt
   git commit -am "New content"
   new_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

   dependency_url="git+file://$PWD"
   ```

2. **Install the old commit in the consumer.**

   ```bash
   cd ../consumer
   npm init -y
   npm config set allow-git=all --location=project
   npm install "dependency@$dependency_url#$old_commit"
   ```

3. **Change `package.json` to request the new commit, then run `npm install`.**

   ```bash
   npm pkg set "dependencies.dependency=$dependency_url#$new_commit"
   npm install
   ```

4. **Check the installed content.**

   ```bash
   cat node_modules/dependency/content.txt
   ```

   **Expected:** `new content`  
   **Actual:** `old content`

   `package-lock.json` also retains the old commit’s SHA.
