body_text:
##### Description

Hibernate Validator 9.1+ deprecates `@Valid` at the container level ([9.1 release notes](https://docs.hibernate.org/validator/9.1/whats-new/en-US/html_single/#_deprecating_the_use_of_valid_at_the_container_level)) and logs at runtime:

> HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (...) is deprecated. You should apply the annotation on the type argument(s).

#24176 already moved `@Valid` to the type argument for `List`/`Set`/`Map` (models and parameters), fixed DTO getters (#24782), list bodies (#24752) and composed (`allOf`/`oneOf`/`anyOf`) array items. **This issue covers the remaining safe gap in the Java Spring generator: model properties wrapped in `Optional` or `JsonNullable`.** Hibernate Validator treats both as containers (`Optional` natively, `JsonNullable` through the `ValueExtractor` registered by `jackson-databind-nullable`), so a member-level `@Valid` still triggers HV000271.

##### Remaining cases (on current `master`)

**1. Model property with `useOptional=true` (field/getter)**

```java
@Valid
@JsonProperty("singleItem")
public Optional<Item> getSingleItem() { ... }
```
→ `HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (java.util.Optional) is deprecated. Affected element: Zoo#getSingleItem()`

**2. Nullable model property with `openApiNullable=true` (field/getter)**

```yaml
nullableSingleItem:
  nullable: true
  allOf:
    - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Item'
```
```java
@Valid
public JsonNullable<Item> getNullableSingleItem() { ... }
```
→ `HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (org.openapitools.jackson.nullable.JsonNullable) is deprecated. Affected element: Zoo#getNullableSingleItem()`

##### Out of scope: optional HTTP parameters

Optional (non-required) model parameters with `useOptional=true` still generate:

```java
@Valid Optional<Item> criteria
@Valid @RequestPart(value = "item", required = false) Optional<Item> item
@Valid @RequestBody(required = false) Optional<Item> item
```
→ `HV000271: ... (java.util.Optional) ... Affected element: SearchApi#searchItems(Animal, Optional)`

These also trigger HV000271. However, they must **not** switch to type-use placement in this issue. With Spring Boot 3 and 4, `Optional<@Valid Item>` causes invalid request body, multipart part and `deepObject` query values to surface as `ConstraintViolationException`, which changes the generated endpoint behavior from HTTP 400 to HTTP 500. Parameter-level `@Valid` preserves the existing Spring MVC 400 response. The immediate functional contract takes precedence over eliminating this warning.

Optional scalar bodies (`@Valid @RequestBody(required = false) Optional<String> body`) have the same warning and remain out of scope for the same reason.

##### Expected

```java
public Optional<@Valid Item> getSingleItem()
public JsonNullable<@Valid Item> getNullableSingleItem()
```

- `@Valid` goes on the type argument only for wrapped **model properties**. Wrapped scalar properties (`Optional<BigDecimal>`, `JsonNullable<String>`, ...) get no `@Valid`.
- Required/non-wrapped single model properties keep member-level `@Valid`.
- Fully qualified type arguments must place the annotation after the qualifier, otherwise the code does not compile: `JsonNullable<com.example.@Valid ExternalModel>` (not `JsonNullable<@Valid com.example.ExternalModel>`), e.g. with `schemaMapping`.

##### Verification

Reproduced with Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate Validator 9.1.3.Final: wrapped generated model properties log HV000271 on `master`; with type-argument placement no warning is logged and nested violations are still reported (`singleItem.code`, ...). For optional HTTP parameters, Spring MVC integration verification showed that type-use placement regresses invalid requests from HTTP 400 to HTTP 500, so this issue intentionally retains the existing output there.

##### openapi-generator version

`master` (after #24176)

##### Related

- #24176 (fix for containers — this issue covers the remaining wrapper cases)
- #24752, #24782 (fixed by #24176)
- #24806

{"repository": "OpenAPITools/openapi-generator", "task_candidate_id": 18657, "repository_id": 195, "issue_number": 25097, "github_issue_id": 5674679670, "html_url": "https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/25097", "created_at": "2026-10-02T08:07:11+00:00", "author_association": "CONTRIBUTOR", "title": "[Bug][Java/Spring] Container-level @Valid on Optional/JsonNullable-wrapped model properties triggers HV000271 (follow-up to #24176)", "body_text": "##### Description

Hibernate Validator 9.1+ deprecates `@Valid` at the container level ([9.1 release notes](https://docs.hibernate.org/validator/9.1/whats-new/en-US/html_single/#_deprecating_the_use_of_valid_at_the_container_level)) and logs at runtime:

> HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (...) is deprecated. You should apply the annotation on the type argument(s).

#24176 already moved `@Valid` to the type argument for `List`/`Set`/`Map` (models and parameters), fixed DTO getters (#24782), list bodies (#24752) and composed (`allOf`/`oneOf`/`anyOf`) array items. **This issue covers the remaining safe gap in the Java Spring generator: model properties wrapped in `Optional` or `JsonNullable`.** Hibernate Validator treats both as containers (`Optional` natively, `JsonNullable` through the `ValueExtractor` registered by `jackson-databind-nullable`), so a member-level `@Valid` still triggers HV000271.

##### Remaining cases (on current `master`)

**1. Model property with `useOptional=true` (field/getter)**

```java
@Valid
@JsonProperty("singleItem")
public Optional<Item> getSingleItem() { ... }
```
→ `HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (java.util.Optional) is deprecated. Affected element: Zoo#getSingleItem()`

**2. Nullable model property with `openApiNullable=true` (field/getter)**

```yaml
nullableSingleItem:
  nullable: true
  allOf:
    - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Item'
```
```java
@Valid
public JsonNullable<Item> getNullableSingleItem() { ... }
```
→ `HV000271: Using @Valid on a container (org.openapitools.jackson.nullable.JsonNullable) is deprecated. Affected element: Zoo#getNullableSingleItem()`

##### Out of scope: optional HTTP parameters

Optional (non-required) model parameters with `useOptional=true` still generate:

```java
@Valid Optional<Item> criteria
@Valid @RequestPart(value = "item", required = false) Optional<Item> item
@Valid @RequestBody(required = false) Optional<Item> item
```
→ `HV000271: ... (java.util.Optional) ... Affected element: SearchApi#searchItems(Animal, Optional)`

These also trigger HV000271. However, they must **not** switch to type-use placement in this issue. With Spring Boot 3 and 4, `Optional<@Valid Item>` causes invalid request body, multipart part and `deepObject` query values to surface as `ConstraintViolationException`, which changes the generated endpoint behavior from HTTP 400 to HTTP 500. Parameter-level `@Valid` preserves the existing Spring MVC 400 response. The immediate functional contract takes precedence over eliminating this warning.

Optional scalar bodies (`@Valid @RequestBody(required = false) Optional<String> body`) have the same warning and remain out of scope for the same reason.

##### Expected

```java
public Optional<@Valid Item> getSingleItem()
public JsonNullable<@Valid Item> getNullableSingleItem()
```

- `@Valid` goes on the type argument only for wrapped **model properties**. Wrapped scalar properties (`Optional<BigDecimal>`, `JsonNullable<String>`, ...) get no `@Valid`.
- Required/non-wrapped single model properties keep member-level `@Valid`.
- Fully qualified type arguments must place the annotation after the qualifier, otherwise the code does not compile: `JsonNullable<com.example.@Valid ExternalModel>` (not `JsonNullable<@Valid com.example.ExternalModel>`), e.g. with `schemaMapping`.

##### Verification

Reproduced with Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate Validator 9.1.3.Final: wrapped generated model properties log HV000271 on `master`; with type-argument placement no warning is logged and nested violations are still reported (`singleItem.code`, ...). For optional HTTP parameters, Spring MVC integration verification showed that type-use placement regresses invalid requests from HTTP 400 to HTTP 500, so this issue intentionally retains the existing output there.

##### openapi-generator version

`master` (after #24176)

##### Related

- #24176 (fix for containers — this issue covers the remaining wrapper cases)
- #24752, #24782 (fixed by #24176)
- #24806

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?
- [ ] [Optional] Sponsorship to speed up the bug fix or feature request ([example](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/6178))

##### Description

The `spring` generator emits annotation attributes that are equal to their default values, which makes the generated API interfaces unnecessarily verbose:

- `required = true` on `@RequestHeader`, `@RequestParam` and `@RequestPart` (`true` is the Spring default for all three). `@CookieValue` and `@RequestBody` already only emit `required = false`.
- `description = ""` on `@Parameter` when the parameter has no description (`""` is the default).
- `description = ""` on `@Operation` (plus an empty ` * ` Javadoc line) when the spec contains an empty description (`description: ''`), because jmustache treats an empty string as truthy in `{{#notes}}`.

This affects all `spring` libraries (spring-boot, spring-cloud, spring-http-interface) and `java-camel`, as they share the same templates.

**Actual output:**

```java
    default ResponseEntity<RedirectResponse> replaceAgreementPaymentCard(
        @NotNull @Parameter(name = "Accept-Language", description = "", required = true, in = ParameterIn.HEADER) @RequestHeader(value = "Accept-Language", required = true) String acceptLanguage,
        @Parameter(name = "id", description = "", required = true, in = ParameterIn.PATH) @PathVariable("id") UUID id,
        @Parameter(name = "ReplaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest", description = "", required = true) @Valid @RequestBody ReplaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest replaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest
    ) {
```

**Expected output** (semantically identical):

```java
    default ResponseEntity<RedirectResponse> replaceAgreementPaymentCard(
        @NotNull @Parameter(name = "Accept-Language", required = true, in = ParameterIn.HEADER) @RequestHeader(value = "Accept-Language") String acceptLanguage,
        @Parameter(name = "id", required = true, in = ParameterIn.PATH) @PathVariable("id") UUID id,
        @Parameter(name = "ReplaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest", required = true) @Valid @RequestBody ReplaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest replaceAgreementPaymentCardRequest
    ) {
```

Note that `required = true` on `@Parameter` must stay, since its default is `false`.

##### openapi-generator version

Latest master (also 7.25.0).

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

Any spec with required header/query/form parameters or parameters without description, e.g. [`modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0/spring/petstore-with-fake-endpoints-models-for-testing.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/master/modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0/spring/petstore-with-fake-endpoints-models-for-testing.yaml) (used by the `samples/server/petstore/springboot` sample).

##### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g spring --library spring-boot -i spec.yaml -o out
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate any `spring` sample, e.g. `./bin/generate-samples.sh bin/configs/spring-boot.yaml`.
2. Look at the generated `*Api.java` interfaces, e.g. `FakeApi.java`: `@RequestHeader(value = "required_boolean_group", required = true)`, `@RequestParam(value = "required_string_group", required = true)`, `@Parameter(name = "...", description = "", ...)`.

##### Related issues/PRs

None found.

##### Suggest a fix

- In `JavaSpring/headerParams.mustache`, `queryParams.mustache` and `formParams.mustache`, only emit `required = false`.
- In `JavaSpring/paramDoc.mustache`, only emit `description` when present.
- In `SpringCodegen`, treat empty operation/parameter descriptions as absent.

I'll open a PR with this change.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

With the C# `generichost` generator, an `anyOf` wrapper with an explicit discriminator mapping reads an object into the correct subtype but serializes the wrapper as `{}`. Every property is lost, including the discriminator.

The concrete subtype serializes correctly using the same generated converters and serializer options. Changing only the schema composition keyword from `anyOf` to `oneOf` makes the wrapper round-trip correctly for both subtypes.

OpenAPI 3.1.1 permits a discriminator alongside `anyOf`: [conditions for using the discriminator object](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html#conditions-for-using-the-discriminator-object).

Expected input and output:

```json
{"type":"image","id":1,"imageUri":"https://example.com/image.jpg"}
```

Actual wrapper output:

```json
{}
```

Verified runtime results:

| Composition | Subtype | Read / concrete subtype write | Wrapper write |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anyOf` + discriminator | Image | Correct | `{}` |
| `anyOf` + discriminator | Document | Correct | `{}` |
| `oneOf` + discriminator | Image | Correct | Original JSON |
| `oneOf` + discriminator | Document | Correct | Original JSON |

Separate scratch experiments also reproduced the failure with the generated client's own DI serializer options on the macOS host and with OpenAPI 3.0.3. Removing the discriminator in another scratch control made the `anyOf` wrapper round-trip both subtypes. These extra controls are not part of the checked-in runner. The actual `{}` output is invalid against `Asset`, because `type` is required.

##### openapi-generator version

- Official `openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:v7.25.0`, the latest stable release checked on 2026-10-06.
- .NET SDK `10.0.401`, actual runtime `10.0.12`, Ubuntu `24.04.5` LTS / Linux ARM64 for generated-client execution.
- Loaded `System.Text.Json` is bundled `10.0.12` from `Microsoft.NETCore.App`, not a separately referenced JSON package.
- The .NET orchestration uses Testcontainers `4.15.0`; host macOS `26.6.2` / ARM64, Docker daemon `29.8.0` / Linux ARM64.
- Generated-client direct packages are `Microsoft.Extensions.Http`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly` and `Microsoft.Net.Http.Headers`, all `10.0.1` emitted by the stock generator.

Also reproduced on current master using `openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:latest@sha256:1f59ca3f11ec33425a9c76591f261e008953644f476ada37799c595cdd1b2b65`. The image reports `7.26.0-SNAPSHOT` and its `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label matches master commit [`3501c8a6684e8b4ce4c82d8c9fef7eb1f5fe91b5`](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/commit/3501c8a6684e8b4ce4c82d8c9fef7eb1f5fe91b5). A fresh scratch copy using that pinned image, with the same schema, generation settings and harness, returned the same four results and bug summary.

For the master run only, a scratch copy changed the generator image selector to accept the pinned `latest@sha256:...` reference above. The checked-in runner accepts released version numbers and does not support `dotnet run -- latest`.

I have not established which release first introduced this behavior.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

Minimal OpenAPI 3.1.1 input: [schema.json](https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-openapitools--openapi-generator-anyof-discriminator-serialization/blob/7179dcfa017304a7f177a9f9b64c270a700b88a3/schema.json).

`Asset` declares `anyOf` with references to `ImageAsset` and `DocumentAsset`. It requires `type` and maps `image` / `document` discriminator values to those schemas. Each subtype requires its corresponding singleton string enum for `type`.

The 7.25.0 CLI validator reports `No validation issues detected.`

##### Generation Details

The .NET/Testcontainers runner executes the equivalent of:

```sh
openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -i schema.json -g csharp -o generated \
  --additional-properties packageName=AnyOfClient,targetFramework=net10.0,library=generichost,nullableReferenceTypes=true,hideGenerationTimestamp=true
```

The control copies the input and replaces `anyOf` with `oneOf`. It changes the package name to `OneOfClient` so both unmodified generated clients can be compiled together. There are no template overrides, modified generated files, or replacement converters.

##### Steps to reproduce

Requires .NET 10 and Docker with Linux containers:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-openapitools--openapi-generator-anyof-discriminator-serialization.git
cd repro-openapitools--openapi-generator-anyof-discriminator-serialization
dotnet run
```

The runner generates both clients in the official generator container and executes a .NET harness in the official SDK container. For each subtype it verifies that the wrapper reader populated the subtype, that serializing the concrete subtype preserves the input, and then that serializing the wrapper preserves it.

Observed output:

```text
SUMMARY BUG REPRODUCED: 2/2 anyOf + discriminator cases write {}; concrete subtype writes and both oneOf controls pass.
```

Require the `SUMMARY BUG REPRODUCED` line and the four `RESULT` lines to confirm this bug. The runner returns `1` when it reproduces with the controls passing, `0` when both wrapper compositions work, and `2` for an unexpected harness, generated-client build or control failure. Exit code `1` alone is not evidence: the host `dotnet run` build can also fail with `1`. Docker or generator infrastructure exceptions terminate the process; the missing-image control returned `134` on this macOS host.

The runner saves generated source and logs under `artifacts/`, including the actual .NET environment and resolved package versions.

##### Related issues/PRs

- [#24398](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/24398) reports empty `oneOf` writers.
- [#23693](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/23693) reports empty `oneOf` writers without a discriminator and working writes with a discriminator.
- [#23261](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/23261) has a similar title but covers a string/null `anyOf` converter accepting and writing only objects.
- Open PRs [#24674](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/pull/24674) and [#24735](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/pull/24735) add writers for `oneOf` without a discriminator. Neither changes the `anyOf` with discriminator path.

The reports and PRs above concern other union-writing failures. This example uses `anyOf` with an explicit discriminator and mapping. I did not find an exact existing report in the issue searches.

##### Suggest a fix

In the generated `AssetJsonConverter`, `Write` opens an object, calls an empty `WriteProperties`, and closes the object. In the `oneOf` control, `Write` instead delegates to the selected subtype's generated `WriteProperties`.

The version-specific [7.25.0 converter template](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/v7.25.0/modules/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/csharp/libraries/generichost/JsonConverter.mustache#L381-L438) supports this observed difference: the discriminator-writing branch iterates `composedSchemas.oneOf`, while the `anyOf` branch is guarded by `{{^model.discriminator}}`. `anyOf` with a discriminator reaches neither subtype-writing branch.

The same branch structure remains in the [tested master source](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/3501c8a6684e8b4ce4c82d8c9fef7eb1f5fe91b5/modules/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/csharp/libraries/generichost/JsonConverter.mustache#L380-L437).

The discriminator path should also handle the mapped `anyOf` subtype. No generator patch has been tested. The `oneOf` control is not proposed as a general replacement for `anyOf`; those compositions can have different validation semantics.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?
- [ ] [Optional] Sponsorship to speed up the bug fix or feature request

##### Description

With `useSourceGeneration=true`, a model referencing two models with nested enums named `TypeEnum` produces `SYSLIB1031`. The generated root context omits metadata for one enum, causing direct serialization of that enum through the context to throw `InvalidOperationException`.

The individual model contexts and their combined resolver work correctly. The demonstrated impact is incomplete metadata when using the root context directly and a build failure when treating the warning as an error.

##### openapi-generator version

Reproduced with stock **7.25.0, 7.26.0, and master 7.27.0-SNAPSHOT (`609b95d`)**, using .NET SDK 10.0.401 and bundled System.Text.Json 10.0.12. Full environment details are in the repro README.

Master was tested using upstream's published Docker image, verified against the current master SHA and pinned by digest. The README records the image and repeatable commands. Whether this is a regression is unknown.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

[Reproduction repository][repro]. The minimal input is `schema.yaml`; the README documents the results and controls.

##### Generation Details

Stock C# `generichost`, `useSourceGeneration=true`, targeting .NET 10. The repository's `generate.sh` contains the exact validation and generation commands. No custom templates or edits to generated code.

Validation succeeds with three unused-model recommendations because the schema has no endpoints.

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the [reproduction repository][repro] and follow its README commands.
2. Observe `SYSLIB1031` during the build.
3. The runner reports one of two nested enum contracts missing and exits `1`. Individual and combined context controls pass with reflection disabled.

Expected: both enum contracts are available through the root context, with no collision warning.

##### Related issues/PRs

No exact duplicate found for `SYSLIB1031`, `TypeInfoPropertyName`, or source-generation enum collisions.

##### Suggest a fix

Generate unique `TypeInfoPropertyName` values for reachable nested enums. This removed the warning and made the same checks pass in a separate control, documented in the README. The reproduction itself retains the failing stock output.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

We use openapi-generator-maven-plugin to generate interfaces for the REST clients, which we then create using RestClient, HttpServiceProxyFactory and org.springframework.aop.framework.ProxyFactory. With useBeanValidation=true this causes validation of the method parameters (because they are annotated @Valid in the generated interface), but it does not validate the response (because it is not annotated @Valid in the generated interface).

## Describe the solution you'd like

Annotate the respones in the generated interfaces with @Valid, including the generic types (e.g. List<@Valid SomeType>).

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Validate the responses using a custom code - this works, but it is a code which could be avoided.

##### Description

With `throwOnAnyError=true` the generated `ApiClient` promises that every failure surfaces as `ApiException`. For a 2xx response whose body matches none of the `oneOf`/`anyOf` variants, `FromJson` throws `InvalidDataException` after the `ErrorException` guard has already passed, so the raw exception reaches the caller without status code, body or headers.

##### openapi-generator version

master (after #25217)

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a csharp client with `--library restsharp --additional-properties throwOnAnyError=true` from a spec where an operation returns a `oneOf` model.
2. Call that operation against a server that returns 200 with a body matching no variant.
3. Observe `InvalidDataException` instead of `ApiException`.

##### Expected behaviour

`ApiException` with `ErrorCode` = 200, `ErrorContent` = raw body, `Headers` populated, and the `InvalidDataException` as `InnerException`.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [ ] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

For operations without a `requestBody`, the `kotlin` client with `library=multiplatform` generates `localVariableBody = io.ktor.client.utils.EmptyContent`. `ApiClient.request` then sets a JSON content type and the body for every `PUT`, `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE`, regardless of whether there is a body:

```kotlin
if (requestConfig.method in listOf(RequestMethod.PUT, RequestMethod.POST, RequestMethod.PATCH, RequestMethod.DELETE)) {
    val contentType = (requestConfig.headers[HttpHeaders.ContentType]?.let { ContentType.parse(it) }
        ?: ContentType.Application.Json)
    this.contentType(contentType)
    this.setBody(body)
}
```

As a result, a `DELETE /items/{id}?row=1` without a request body goes out with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Content-Length: 0`. Servers that bind a JSON body whenever the content type says JSON reject the request. ASP.NET Core with FastEndpoints answers:

```json
{"statusCode":400,"message":"One or more errors occurred!","errors":{"/SerializerErrors":["The input does not contain any JSON tokens. Expected the input to start with a valid JSON token, when isFinalBlock is true. LineNumber: 0 | BytePositionInLine: 0."]}}
```

The same `DELETE` succeeds when the client omits the `Content-Type` header. `DELETE` operations that do declare a JSON `requestBody` work as expected.

The same block exists in `libraries/jvm-ktor/infrastructure/ApiClient.kt.mustache`.

##### openapi-generator version

7.25.0 (Gradle plugin `org.openapi.generator`). The same code is in the 7.26.0 templates and on `master` (`modules/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/kotlin-client/libraries/multiplatform/infrastructure/ApiClient.kt.mustache`, the `request` function). Not a regression as far as I can tell.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Delete without body
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /items/{id}:
    delete:
      operationId: deleteItem
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: rowVersion
          in: query
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Deleted
```

##### Generation Details

```
generatorName: kotlin
library: multiplatform
additionalProperties:
  dateLibrary: kotlinx-datetime
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the client from the spec above with `-g kotlin --library multiplatform`.
2. Call `deleteItem("1", 1)` against any server, or a request logger.
3. Observe the request headers: `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Length: 0`.

Actual: a JSON content type is sent although the operation has no request body.
Expected: no `Content-Type` header (and no body) when the operation declares no `requestBody`.

##### Related issues/PRs

None found (searched for "multiplatform DELETE content-type empty body" and "EmptyContent Content-Type").

##### Suggest a fix

Only set the content type and body when there is a body, for example:

```kotlin

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator? (`openapi-generator-cli validate`: "No validation issues detected.")
- [x] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists? (`7.27.0-SNAPSHOT`, commit 3faf172)
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs? (see below)
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?
- [ ] [Optional] Sponsorship to speed up the bug fix or feature request ([example](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/6178))

##### Description

When all the schemas mapped by a oneOf discriminator declare the discriminator property as a `$ref` to the same *primitive alias* schema (here `ShapeKind`: a plain `type: string` schema without `enum`), the generated oneOf interface declares the getter with the **name of the alias schema** (`ShapeKind getKind()`). No model is generated for a primitive alias, and the implementing classes correctly use `String`, so the generated code does not compile (`cannot find symbol`).

7.25.0 generates `String getKind()`. This looks like a side effect of #24812: when only one distinct property schema remains and it is a `$ref`, `DefaultCodegen#getCommonSchemaType` returns `toModelName(<ref>)` without checking that a model exists for it.

Affected generators (tested): `spring` (with default options), `jaxrs-spec` and `java` (`--library restclient` / `resttemplate`) with `useOneOfInterfaces=true`. Not affected (tested with default options): `kotlin`, `kotlin-spring`.

##### openapi-generator version

7.26.0. It is a regression: 7.25.0 is fine. Still reproducible with the latest snapshot (`7.27.0-SNAPSHOT`, commit 3faf172).

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

<details><summary>shapes.yaml</summary>

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Discriminator property typed by a primitive alias
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /shape:
    get:
      operationId: getShape
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A shape
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Shape'
components:
  schemas:
    Shape:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Circle'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Square'
      discriminator:
        propertyName: kind
        mapping:
          circle: '#/components/schemas/Circle'
          square: '#/components/schemas/Square'
    ShapeKind:
      type: string
      description: The kind of shape.
    Circle:
      type: object
      required:
        - kind
      properties:
        kind:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShapeKind'
        radius:
          type: number
    Square:
      type: object
      required:
        - kind
      properties:
        kind:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShapeKind'
        side:
          type: number
```

</details>

##### Generation Details

```bash
java -jar openapi-generator-cli-7.26.0.jar generate -g spring -i shapes.yaml -o out --global-property models
```

No additional options are needed (JDK 21). The same happens with `-g jaxrs-spec --additional-properties useOneOfInterfaces=true` or `-g java --library restclient --additional-properties useOneOfInterfaces=true`.

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate as above with 7.26.0 (and with 7.25.0 for comparison).
2. Look at `out/src/main/java/org/openapitools/model/Shape.java`.

   7.25.0:

   ```java
   public interface Shape {
       public String getKind();
   }
   ```

   7.26.0:

   ```java
   public interface Shape {
       public ShapeKind getKind();
   }
   ```

   There is no `ShapeKind.java` (only `Shape`, `Circle` and `Square` are generated), and `Circle` / `Square` use `String getKind()`.
3. Compiling the generated sources fails:

   ```
   org/openapitools/model/Shape.java:37: error: cannot find symbol
       public ShapeKind getKind();
              ^
     symbol:   class ShapeKind
     location: interface Shape
   ```

Observations that narrow the cause:

- It only happens when the discriminator property resolves to exactly **one distinct schema** across all the mapped subtypes. If each subtype references its *own* alias schema, the output is fine (`String getKind()`): that goes through the multi-schema branch of `getCommonSchemaType`, which dereferences the `$ref`s first.
- It also happens when the alias property is inherited through `allOf` from a shared base schema.
- An integer alias (`type: integer`) or a `format: uuid` alias fails the same way.

##### Related issues/PRs

- #24812 (merged 2026-09-06): introduced `getCommonSchemaType` / `DiscriminatorUtils.getDistinctTypes`. "Matching `$ref` types are used" assumes that a model exists for every `$ref`.
- #24950 / #25008: another regression from the same change (`format: enum` mapped to `Enum`), different trigger.
- #24769, #19194, #24959: the non-`String` discriminator problems that #24812 fixes. The fix suggested below keeps that behavior.
- #24156 (open): also touches discriminator type resolution, possibly overlapping.

I could not find an existing issue or PR about discriminators typed by a primitive alias.

##### Suggest a fix

In `DefaultCodegen#getCommonSchemaType` (`case 1`), when the only distinct property schema is a `$ref`, resolve aliases of primitive types first before treating the `$ref` as a model name. This mirrors `getSingleSchemaType`, which computes the property type of the implementing classes: `unaliasSchema`, then the model name if a `$ref` remains, otherwise the primitive type:

```diff
                 Schema first = schemas.get(0);
                 try {
                     if (StringUtils.isNotEmpty(first.get$ref())) {
+                        // a $ref to an alias of a primitive type has no model: use the aliased type,
+                        // like the type of the property in the concrete models
+                        first = unaliasSchema(first);
+                    }
+                    if (StringUtils.isNotEmpty(first.get$ref())) {
                         return toModelName(ModelUtils.getSimpleRef(first.get$ref()));
                     }
```

`unaliasSchema` keeps the `$ref` for everything that gets a generated model (enums, objects, composed schemas, `schemaMappings` targets), so the existing behavior for those is unchanged. Primitive aliases (also alias of alias) are resolved to the underlying schema and handled like an inline property (`String`, `Integer`, `UUID`, ...), consistent with the implementing classes. It does not touch the lines changed by #25008.

Validation of the patch (patched `DefaultCodegen`, compiled against the 7.26.0 jar; the file is identical on master):

- The reproduction above generates `String getKind()` for `spring`, `jaxrs-spec` and `java` (`restclient`, `resttemplate`); the generated `spring` and `restclient` model sources compile with javac.
- A spec with six oneOf groups compiles with javac: integer alias -> `Integer`, `format: uuid` alias -> `UUID`, alias of an alias -> `String`, alias of an enum -> the enum model, direct `$ref` to an enum -> the enum model (unchanged from 7.26.0), inline string -> `String`. For comparison, the same spec gives 16 compile errors with 7.25.0 (non-`String` discriminators, the problem fixed by #24812) and 4 with 7.26.0 (the alias groups).
- Generating the 150 test specs that mention `discriminator` (`modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0` and `3_1`) with `spring` and with `java --library restclient` (both with `useOneOfInterfaces=true`) gives byte-identical output with and without the patch. None of them exercises a primitive-alias discriminator, so a regression test would be new coverage.

Happy to open a PR with the change and a regression test if this approach looks right.

##### Description

When all the schemas mapped by a oneOf discriminator declare the discriminator property as a `$ref` to the same *primitive alias* schema (here `ShapeKind`: a plain `type: string` schema without `enum`), the generated oneOf interface declares the getter with the **name of the alias schema** (`ShapeKind getKind()`). No model is generated for a primitive alias, and the implementing classes correctly use `String`, so the generated code does not compile (`cannot find symbol`).

7.25.0 generates `String getKind()`. This looks like a side effect of #24812: when only one distinct property schema remains and it is a `$ref`, `DefaultCodegen#getCommonSchemaType` returns `toModelName(<ref>)` without checking that a model exists for it.

Affected generators (tested): `spring` (with default options), `jaxrs-spec` and `java` (`--library restclient` / `resttemplate`) with `useOneOfInterfaces=true`. Not affected (tested with default options): `kotlin`, `kotlin-spring`.

##### openapi-generator version

7.26.0. It is a regression: 7.25.0 is fine. Still reproducible with the latest snapshot (`7.27.0-SNAPSHOT`, commit 3faf172).

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

<details><summary>shapes.yaml</summary>

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Discriminator property typed by a primitive alias
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /shape:
    get:
      operationId: getShape
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A shape
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Shape'
components:
  schemas:
    Shape:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Circle'
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Square'
      discriminator:
        propertyName: kind
        mapping:
          circle: '#/components/schemas/Circle'
          square: '#/components/schemas/Square'
    ShapeKind:
      type: string
      description: The kind of shape.
    Circle:
      type: object
      required:
        - kind
      properties:
        kind:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShapeKind'
        radius:
          type: number
    Square:
      type: object
      required:
        - kind
      properties:
        kind:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ShapeKind'
        side:
          type: number
```

</details>

##### Generation Details

```bash
java -jar openapi-generator-cli-7.26.0.jar generate -g spring -i shapes.yaml -o out --global-property models
```

No additional options are needed (JDK 21). The same happens with `-g jaxrs-spec --additional-properties useOneOfInterfaces=true` or `-g java --library restclient --additional-properties useOneOfInterfaces=true`.

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate as above with 7.26.0 (and with 7.25.0 for comparison).
2. Look at `out/src/main/java/org/openapitools/model/Shape.java`.

   7.25.0:

   ```java
   public interface Shape {
       public String getKind();
   }
   ```

   7.26.0:

   ```java
   public interface Shape {
       public ShapeKind getKind();
   }
   ```

   There is no `ShapeKind.java` (only `Shape`, `Circle` and `Square` are generated), and `Circle` / `Square` use `String getKind()`.
3. Compiling the generated sources fails:

   ```
   org/openapitools/model/Shape.java:37: error: cannot find symbol
       public ShapeKind getKind();
              ^
     symbol:   class ShapeKind
     location: interface Shape
   ```

Observations that narrow the cause:

- It only happens when the discriminator property resolves to exactly **one distinct schema** across all the mapped subtypes. If each subtype references its *own* alias schema, the output is fine (`String getKind()`): that goes through the multi-schema branch of `getCommonSchemaType`, which dereferences the `$ref`s first.
- It also happens when the alias property is inherited through `allOf` from a shared base schema.
- An integer alias (`type: integer`) or a `format: uuid` alias fails the same way.

##### Related issues/PRs

- #24812 (merged 2026-09-06): introduced `getCommonSchemaType` / `DiscriminatorUtils.getDistinctTypes`. "Matching `$ref` types are used" assumes that a model exists for every `$ref`.
- #24950 / #25008: another regression from the same change (`format: enum` mapped to `Enum`), different trigger.
- #24769, #19194, #24959: the non-`String` discriminator problems that #24812 fixes. The fix suggested below keeps that behavior.
- #24156 (open): also touches discriminator type resolution, possibly overlapping.

I could not find an existing issue or PR about discriminators typed by a primitive alias.

##### Suggest a fix

In `DefaultCodegen#getCommonSchemaType` (`case 1`), when the only distinct property schema is a `$ref`, resolve aliases of primitive types first before treating the `$ref` as a model name. This mirrors `getSingleSchemaType`, which computes the property type of the implementing classes: `unaliasSchema`, then the model name if a `$ref` remains, otherwise the primitive type:

```diff
                 Schema first = schemas.get(0);
                 try {
                     if (StringUtils.isNotEmpty(first.get$ref())) {
+                        // a $ref to an alias of a primitive type has no model: use the aliased type,
+                        // like the type of the property in the concrete models
+                        first = unaliasSchema(first);
+                    }
+                    if (StringUtils.isNotEmpty(first.get$ref())) {
                         return toModelName(ModelUtils.getSimpleRef(first.get$ref()));
                     }
```

`unaliasSchema` keeps the `$ref` for everything that gets a generated model (enums, objects, composed schemas, `schemaMappings` targets), so the existing behavior for those is unchanged. Primitive aliases (also alias of alias) are resolved to the underlying schema and handled like an inline property (`String`, `Integer`, `UUID`, ...), consistent with the implementing classes. It does not touch the lines changed by #25008.

Validation of the patch (patched `DefaultCodegen`, compiled against the 7.26.0 jar; the file is identical on master):

- The reproduction above generates `String getKind()` for `spring`, `jaxrs-spec` and `java` (`restclient`, `resttemplate`); the generated `spring` and `restclient` model sources compile with javac.
- A spec with six oneOf groups compiles with javac: integer alias -> `Integer`, `format: uuid` alias -> `UUID`, alias of an alias -> `String`, alias of an enum -> the enum model, direct `$ref` to an enum -> the enum model (unchanged from 7.26.0), inline string -> `String`. For comparison, the same spec gives 16 compile errors with 7.25.0 (non-`String` discriminators, the problem fixed by #24812) and 4 with 7.26.0 (the alias groups).
- Generating the 150 test specs that mention `discriminator` (`modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0` and `3_1`) with `spring` and with `java --library restclient` (both with `useOneOfInterfaces=true`) gives byte-identical output with and without the patch. None of them exercises a primitive-alias discriminator, so a regression test would be new coverage.

Happy to open a PR with the change and a regression test if this approach looks right.

### Summary

`OpenApiEvaluator.validate(OpenAPI)` reports unused schemas (`Unused model: <name>`) even when recommendations are globally disabled (`RuleConfiguration.isEnableRecommendations() == false`). All other recommendations respect this flag: default not in enum, header with underscore, and GET/HEAD with request body. Only the unused-schema check ignores it. Recommendations are optional best-practice warnings that the evaluator should emit only when recommendations are enabled.

### Environment

- Project: OpenAPI Generator v7.25.0 (fork), commit `ef964b04480889ef86b56cfae84ade8ad4c91c41`
- Module: `modules/openapi-generator`
- Class/method: `org.openapitools.codegen.validations.oas.OpenApiEvaluator#validate(OpenAPI)`
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic (amd64)
- Java: OpenJDK 25 (compiled with source/target 11)
- Tests: JUnit 5.10.2 + Mockito 4.10.0, run with the Maven Wrapper (Surefire 3.2.5)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an OpenAPI 3.0 document with a schema under `components/schemas` that is not referenced anywhere (e.g. `Orphan`).
2. Create a `RuleConfiguration` with `isEnableRecommendations() = false` and `isEnableUnusedSchemasRecommendation() = true` (the default).
3. Call `new OpenApiEvaluator(config).validate(openAPI)`.
4. Inspect `getWarnings()` on the result.

Automated test case: **CT-OE-07** (`OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest.ct07GlobalRecommendationsOffSuppressUnusedSchema`).

```
./mvnw -pl modules/openapi-generator -am test -Dtest=OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
```

### Expected result

No recommendation warnings, since recommendations are globally disabled.

### Actual result

```
unused-schema recommendation emitted while recommendations are disabled: [Unused model: Orphan]
==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

The failure occurred in all 3 Surefire attempts (`rerunFailingTestsCount = 2`), so it is not flaky.

### Root cause

In `OpenApiEvaluator.java`, line 46, the unused-schema block checks only its own flag:

```java
if (ruleConfiguration.isEnableUnusedSchemasRecommendation()) {
```

The default-not-in-enum rule (line 61) and the delegated validators (`OpenApiSchemaValidations`, `OpenApiParameterValidations`, `OpenApiOperationValidations`, `OpenApiSecuritySchemeValidations`) all check the global `isEnableRecommendations()` flag first.

### Impact

- The CLI `validate` command without `--recommend` calls `setEnableRecommendations(false)` (`Validate.java`, lines 71–72). It still lists unused schemas as warnings and ends with "Spec has N recommendation(s)".
- The Maven plugin's `validate` goal also disables recommendations (`ValidateMojo.java`, line 377). From reading the code, with `strictSpec = true` a single unused schema is enough to fail the goal (lines 245 and 252). *This plugin behavior was identified by code reading only and was not executed.*

### Suggested fix

Require both flags, as the default-not-in-enum rule does:

```java
if (ruleConfiguration.isEnableRecommendations()
        && ruleConfiguration.isEnableUnusedSchemasRecommendation()) {
```

### Summary

The "Schema has default value not in enum" recommendation compares the `default` against the `enum` items with `List.contains`. In numeric schemas the values are `BigDecimal`, and `BigDecimal.equals` takes the scale into account. As a result, `1.50` is not recognized as equal to `1.5`, and the evaluator emits a false warning.

### Environment

- Project: OpenAPI Generator v7.25.0 (fork), commit `ef964b04480889ef86b56cfae84ade8ad4c91c41`
- Module: `modules/openapi-generator`
- Class/method: `org.openapitools.codegen.validations.oas.OpenApiEvaluator#validate(OpenAPI)`
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic (amd64)
- Java: OpenJDK 25 (compiled with source/target 11)
- Tests: JUnit 5.10.2 + Mockito 4.10.0, run with the Maven Wrapper (Surefire 3.2.5)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an OpenAPI 3.0 document with a schema `Rate` that has a `number` property `factor` with `enum: [1.5]` and `default: 1.50` (a `NumberSchema` with `new BigDecimal("1.5")` in the enum and `new BigDecimal("1.50")` as the default).
2. Create a `RuleConfiguration` with `isEnableRecommendations() = true` and `isEnableDefaultNotInEnumRecommendation() = true`.
3. Call `new OpenApiEvaluator(config).validate(openAPI)`.
4. Inspect `getWarnings()` on the result.

Automated test case: **CT-OE-14** (`OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest.ct14NumericDefaultComparedByValue`).

```
./mvnw -pl modules/openapi-generator -am test -Dtest=OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
```

### Expected result

No warning: 1.50 and 1.5 are the same number, so the default belongs to the enum.

### Actual result

```
1.50 reported as outside enum [1.5]: [Schema has default value '1.50' not in enum [1.5]]
==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

The failure occurred in all 3 Surefire attempts (`rerunFailingTestsCount = 2`), so it is not flaky.

### Root cause

In `OpenApiEvaluator.java`, line 73:

```java
&& !enumList.contains(defaultValue)) {
```

`List.contains` relies on `equals`. For `BigDecimal`, `new BigDecimal("1.5").equals(new BigDecimal("1.50"))` returns `false`, while `compareTo` returns `0`.

### Impact

Users get a false recommendation and may "fix" a default that is already correct. The defect was reproduced with a model built in memory (unit test). *It was not verified whether swagger-parser preserves the scale when reading a YAML/JSON file written with a different number of decimal places (e.g. `1.50`).*

### Suggested fix

Compare numeric values by value and keep `equals` for every other type. For example:

```java
boolean inEnum = enumList.stream().anyMatch(item ->
        (item instanceof BigDecimal && defaultValue instanceof BigDecimal)
                ? ((BigDecimal) item).compareTo((BigDecimal) defaultValue) == 0
                : Objects.equals(item, defaultValue));
```

1. Create an OpenAPI 3.0 document with a schema `Rate` that has a `number` property `factor` with `enum: [1.5]` and `default: 1.50` (a `NumberSchema` with `new BigDecimal("1.5")` in the enum and `new BigDecimal("1.50")` as the default).
2. Create a `RuleConfiguration` with `isEnableRecommendations() = true` and `isEnableDefaultNotInEnumRecommendation() = true`.
3. Call `new OpenApiEvaluator(config).validate(openAPI)`.
4. Inspect `getWarnings()` on the result.

Automated test case: **CT-OE-14** (`OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest.ct14NumericDefaultComparedByValue`).

```
./mvnw -pl modules/openapi-generator -am test -Dtest=OpenApiEvaluatorJUnitTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
```

### Expected result

No warning: 1.50 and 1.5 are the same number, so the default belongs to the enum.

### Actual result

```
1.50 reported as outside enum [1.5]: [Schema has default value '1.50' not in enum [1.5]]
==> expected: <true> but was: <false>
```

The failure occurred in all 3 Surefire attempts (`rerunFailingTestsCount = 2`), so it is not flaky.

### Root cause

In `OpenApiEvaluator.java`, line 73:

```java
&& !enumList.contains(defaultValue)) {
```

`List.contains` relies on `equals`. For `BigDecimal`, `new BigDecimal("1.5").equals(new BigDecimal("1.50"))` returns `false`, while `compareTo` returns `0`.

### Impact

Users get a false recommendation and may "fix" a default that is already correct. The defect was reproduced with a model built in memory (unit test). *It was not verified whether swagger-parser preserves the scale when reading a YAML/JSON file written with a different number of decimal places (e.g. `1.50`).*

### Suggested fix

Compare numeric values by value and keep `equals` for every other type. For example:

```java
boolean inEnum = enumList.stream().anyMatch(item ->
        (item instanceof BigDecimal && defaultValue instanceof BigDecimal)
                ? ((BigDecimal) item).compareTo((BigDecimal) defaultValue) == 0
                : Objects.equals(item, defaultValue));
```

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

Examples generated by `ExampleGenerator` for numeric schemas are not valid instances of the schema in two situations:

1. Only `maximum` is set and it is negative. `randomNumber(min, max)` returns `random.nextDouble() * max`, which lies in `(max, 0]` when `max < 0`. With `maximum: -5` the generated example is `0` (integer) or `-0.4004...` (number).
2. `exclusiveMinimum` / `exclusiveMaximum` are never read. For `type: integer, minimum: 0, exclusiveMinimum: true`, the generated value is `random.nextDouble() + 0` truncated to `int`, which is always `0`.

The OpenAPI 3.0.3 Schema Object defines `example` as "an example of an instance for this schema". `maximum`/`exclusiveMinimum` follow JSON Schema Validation (wright-00, 5.2–5.5). The generated examples end up in HTML/Markdown docs and in server stubs (`JavaSpring`, `java-wiremock`, `aspnetcore`), where they fail validation against the spec they came from.

##### openapi-generator version

7.25.0 (also current `master`).

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info: {title: repro, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /temperature:
    get:
      responses:
        '200':
          description: ok
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Reading'
components:
  schemas:
    Reading:
      type: object
      properties:
        celsius:
          type: integer
          maximum: -5
        level:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
          exclusiveMinimum: true
```

##### Generation Details / Steps to reproduce

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g html -i repro.yaml -o out
```

Actual "Example data": `{"celsius" : 0, "level" : 0}`.
Expected: `celsius <= -5` and `level > 0`.

##### Suggest a fix

In `randomNumber`, when only `max` is set, use `max - random.nextDouble()` (or an offset below `max`). Read `getExclusiveMinimum()` / `getExclusiveMaximum()` (and `exclusiveMinimumValue` / `exclusiveMaximumValue` for 3.1), and nudge integer bounds by 1 when they are exclusive.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

`resolvePropertyToExample` returns the Java string literal `"{}"` for an object schema without properties and for a `$ref` that cannot be resolved. `Json.pretty` then serializes it as a JSON **string** (`"metadata" : "{}"`) instead of an empty object (`"metadata" : { }`), so the example has the wrong type (JSON Schema Validation wright-00, 5.21).

The same happens one level up. For a top-level model `type: object` without `properties`, `resolveModelToExample` falls through to `return null`, and `generate(null, ["application/json"], "Anything")` returns the example `null`. Through the CLI this model gets unaliased first, so the operation simply has no example; only programmatic callers see `null`.

##### openapi-generator version

7.25.0 (also current `master`).

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
components:
  schemas:
    Reading:
      type: object
      properties:
        metadata:
          type: object
```

##### Steps to reproduce

`generate -g html` → "Example data" shows `"metadata" : "{}"`. Expected: `"metadata" : { }`.

##### Suggest a fix

Return `new LinkedHashMap<>()` (an empty map) instead of the string `"{}"` in both branches of `resolvePropertyToExample`, and also for object schemas without properties in `resolveModelToExample`.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [ ] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [ ] Have you tested with a locally built latest-master generator?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

The `typescript-fetch` runtime requires browser-specific type names even in a Node application that already provides native fetch and its types through `@types/node`.

In particular, `FetchAPI = WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope['fetch']` depends on a browser/worker global interface, and the runtime also refers to the standalone `RequestCredentials` type. Neither name is supplied by Node's fetch declarations, although `fetch`, `RequestInit`, `Response` and `FormData` are available.

This matters when a generated SDK is consumed by a Node-only TypeScript project. Building the SDK itself with DOM types does not declare that requirement for its consumers. Source consumers fail compilation, and declaration consumers can also fail when library checking is enabled.

Our workaround is to add `/// <reference lib="dom" preserve="true" />` at the SDK package entry point. That makes compilation succeed, but introduces the entire DOM type environment into consuming server projects, including browser globals that do not exist at runtime.

Expected: a generated client should be able to use the platform's existing fetch types in a modern Node-only project without requiring the full DOM library.

##### openapi-generator version

Our client was generated with 7.15.0.

The same browser-specific references remain in the current master runtime template. I also compiled the current checked-in master Petstore runtime and reproduced the failure. Its fetched Git blob SHA was `b78ab39fffb6aa6f0ab60c9ca2fa700f2fc2d8d7`.

I have not built the latest-master generator JAR, so the corresponding checklist item is intentionally unchecked.

Type-check environment: TypeScript 6.0.2, `@types/node` 24.19.1; Node v25.8.2. The failure concerns type declarations rather than fetch availability at runtime.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

The problem is in the shared runtime and does not depend on a particular schema. A minimal input for generation is:

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.0.3",
  "info": { "title": "Reproduction", "version": "1.0.0" },
  "paths": { "/ping": { "get": { "operationId": "ping", "responses": { "204": { "description": "No content" } } } } }
}
```

##### Generation Details

```sh
openapi-generator-cli generate -g typescript-fetch -i openapi.json -o generated --additional-properties=supportsES6=true
```

Alternatively, the current checked-in upstream sample provides a reproduction without building the generator:

https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/master/samples/client/petstore/typescript-fetch/builds/default/runtime.ts

##### Steps to reproduce

1. In a scratch TypeScript project with TypeScript and `@types/node` installed, copy the upstream sample `runtime.ts` above.
2. Compile it with the following configuration:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2023",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "lib": ["ES2023"],
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false,
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "files": ["runtime.ts"]
}
```

3. Run `tsc -p tsconfig.json`.

Actual result: six diagnostics, including three missing `RequestCredentials` references, one missing `WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope` reference, and two cascading response-type errors.

4. Add `"DOM"` to `lib`, or prepend `/// <reference lib="dom" preserve="true" />` to `runtime.ts`. The same runtime then compiles with zero diagnostics.

##### Related issues/PRs

I searched issues and PRs for `WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`, `RequestCredentials`, and `typescript-fetch` combined with DOM/Node terms, and did not find an exact match.

#3798 and #3801 explain the historical replacement of `GlobalFetch` with `WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope` for TypeScript 3.6 compatibility; this report concerns native-fetch Node consumers.

##### Suggest a fix

Consider replacing browser-specific aliases in `typescript-fetch/runtime.mustache` with types derived from APIs shared by browsers and Node:

- Derive credentials from `NonNullable<RequestInit['credentials']>`.
- Define the fetch callback contract without referencing `WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`, while preserving compatibility with injected fetch implementations and middleware.

An isolated prototype using `(url: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>` for the fetch callback and the credentials type above compiled the current runtime with zero diagnostics both with Node-only types and with Node plus DOM types. This is an illustrative prototype, not a compatibility-verified final patch: the public callback signature needs review before narrowing it.

Simply changing the alias to `typeof globalThis.fetch` introduces strict function-assignability errors for the runtime's narrower middleware callback, so a one-line alias replacement is insufficient.

A fix should include compilation coverage for Node without DOM, existing browser configurations, injected fetch implementations, middleware, and emitted declarations consumed by a separate Node project. Would this platform-neutral direction be acceptable for a focused PR?

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue? (generated with the 7.26.0 CLI jar from Maven Central)
- [ ] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator? (the generator's own validation passes with `skipValidateSpec=false`)
- [ ] Have you tested with the latest master? (tested with the 7.26.0 release only, not a master build)
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

After #24176 (in 7.26.0), Hibernate Validator 9.1 no longer warns for `Optional` query params, but HV000271 is still logged for non-required `@RequestBody` params. The `spring` generator still emits `@Valid` outside the `Optional`:

```java
ResponseEntity<Void> createFoo(
    @Parameter(name = "FooRequest", description = "") @Valid @RequestBody(required = false) Optional<FooRequest> fooRequest
);
```

```

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Minimal spec provided.
- [x] Input validated by the generator.
- [x] Reproduced on current master (`1fdc3307942fcf853990cda8701d71c7e0753157`).

##### Description

The `rust-axum` generator ignores explicit `additionalProperties: false` when generating object models. The resulting Serde structs silently accept and discard unknown JSON keys, even though the schema prohibits them.

##### openapi-generator version

Reproduced with 7.23.0, 7.26.0, and current master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT). The regression test on master fails because the generated `ClosedObject` struct lacks `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`.

##### OpenAPI declaration

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info: {title: Closed object test, version: 1.0.0}
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Request:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [name]
      properties: {name: {type: string}}
```

##### Generation and reproduction

Generate using `-g rust-axum -i closed-object.yaml -o generated`.

The generated `Request` derives `serde::Deserialize` but has no `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Consequently, `serde_json::from_str::<Request>(r#"{"name":"example","unexpected":true}"#)` succeeds. It should return an unknown-field error. A body containing only the declared `name` field should still deserialize successfully.

##### Related issues and proposed fix

No matching rust-axum fix was found in searches for `deny_unknown_fields` and `rust-axum additionalProperties`. This is separate from support for retaining additional properties alongside declared fields.

Emit `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on generated object structs when the schema explicitly sets `additionalProperties: false`. Keep the existing behavior for omitted, true, and schema-valued settings. Add generator-output assertions and Rust deserialization tests covering closed objects, nested closed objects, objects whose declared fields are optional, and free-form configuration inside a declared field.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Minimal spec provided and validated with the CLI.
- [x] Reproduced on latest master (`1fdc3307942fcf853990cda8701d71c7e0753157`).
- [x] Searched open and closed issues and PRs.
- [x] Actual and expected output provided below.

##### Description

With the Rust server generator's `validate` feature, a root model's `serde_valid::Validate` call can return success when a nested model is invalid. Generated array newtypes derive `Validate`, but their inner fields do not have `#[validate]`. Named `oneOf`/`anyOf` newtypes have the same missing recursion step. Object fields also omit nested validation when they have length or item bounds.

This makes a root validation call unreliable as a structural validation boundary. Applications must walk generated model graphs by hand to find invalid children.

##### OpenAPI Generator version

Latest master, built locally at `1fdc3307942fcf853990cda8701d71c7e0753157`. The array-wrapper case also applies to 7.22.0 and 7.26.0.

##### Minimal OpenAPI definition

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Nested validation
  version: '1.0'
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Positive:
      type: object
      required: [value]
      properties:
        value:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
    Positives:
      type: array
      items:
        $ref: '#/components/schemas/Positive'
    Parent:
      type: object
      required: [children]
      properties:
        children:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Positives'
```

##### Generation and reproduction

Generate with:

```sh
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate \
  -g rust-server -i nested.yaml --generate-alias-as-model \
  --additional-properties packageName=recursive_validation -o generated
```

Add this integration test and run `cargo test --no-default-features --features validate --test recursive_validation`:

```rust
use recursive_validation::models::{Parent, Positive, Positives};
use serde_valid::Validate;

#[test]
fn root_validation_reaches_array_items() {
    let root = Parent {
        children: Positives::from(vec![Positive { value: 0 }]),
    };
    assert!(root.validate().is_err());
}
```

Actual: the assertion fails because validation returns `Ok(())`. Expected: the root reports the child's `minimum` violation.

##### Proposed fix

Generate recursion through model-valued wrapper fields and keep recursive validation when a field also has collection bounds. Primitive-valued wrappers and primitive union alternatives must still compile; Rust primitives such as `String` do not implement `serde_valid::Validate`.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [X] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [X] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [X] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
- [X] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [X] What's the actual output vs expected output?
- [ ] [Optional] Sponsorship to speed up the bug fix or feature request ([example](https://redirect.github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/6178))

<!--
Please follow the issue template below for bug reports.
Also please indicate in the issue title which language/library is concerned. E.g.:  [BUG][JAVA] Bug generating foo with bar 
-->

##### Description

When a `string` property's `pattern` constraint contains a JSON `\u00XX`-style escape for a
C0/C1 control code point (e.g. to explicitly forbid control characters in a free-text field,
a common and legitimate validation use case), the Go client generator copies the **decoded**
pattern value directly into the generated `validate:"regexp=..."` struct tag without
re-escaping it for Go source syntax.

Go disallows a literal NUL character — and
most other control characters — anywhere in source code, including inside string and raw
(backtick) string literals, so the generated file fails to compile / fails `gofmt` with:

```
illegal character NUL
```

This is the same code path that was previously patched for two other unsafe characters:
backtick (fixed in #19358, closing #19102) and comma (fixed in #24349, closing #20079).

##### openapi-generator version

Reproduced end-to-end (actual Go codegen run + `gofmt`) against **v7.25.0**. The affected
code in `AbstractGoCodegen.java` in the latest release **v7.26.0** (2026-10-06) and on `master` as of 2026-10-14, so
this still affects the current release.


##### OpenAPI declaration file content

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: control-char-pattern-repro
  version: "1.0"
paths:
  /ping:
    get:
      operationId: ping
      responses:
        "200":
          description: ok
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/TestModel"
components:
  schemas:
    TestModel:
      type: object
      properties:
        key:
          type: string
          # NOTE: as written here, this YAML/JSON "\u0000" is the standard (and only
          # valid) way to express the NUL code point in a JSON Schema pattern string.
          # It decodes to a literal control character when the spec is parsed.
          pattern: "^[^\u0000-\u001f]+$"
```

(equivalent minimal JSON spec, for convenience:)

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.0.3",
  "info": { "title": "control-char-pattern-repro", "version": "1.0" },
  "paths": {
    "/ping": {
      "get": {
        "operationId": "ping",
        "responses": {
          "200": {
            "description": "ok",
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/TestModel" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "TestModel": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "key": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^[^\u0000-\u001f]+$"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Generation Details

```shell
openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -g go \
  --input-spec spec.json \
  --output out \
  --package-name testapi \
  --enable-post-process-file \
  --global-property apis,models,modelTests=true,modelDocs=false,apiDocs=false,supportingFiles,apiTests=false
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the command above against the spec.
2. Run `gofmt -l out/model_test_model.go` (or just try to `go build`).
3. Observe:
   ```
   out/model_test_model.go:22:82: illegal character NUL
   ```
##### Actual vs expected output

Generated struct field (actual — contains two raw, non-printable bytes: 0x00 and 0x1F,
shown below as `<NUL>`/`<US>` since they are not renderable in this markdown file):

```go
Key *string `json:"key,omitempty" validate:"regexp=^[^<NUL>-<US>]+$"`
```

Expected — the pattern's control-character escapes should be re-escaped as literal Go/regex
escape text when written into the struct tag, e.g.:

```go
Key *string `json:"key,omitempty" validate:"regexp=^[^\x00-\x1f]+$"`
```

(Go's own `regexp` package correctly understands `\x00`-style hex escapes inside the pattern
text, so this would both compile and preserve the original validation semantics.)

##### Related issues/PRs

- #19102 / #19358 — backtick in pattern breaks generated code (fixed, same code block)
- #20079 / #24349 — comma in pattern breaks `validate` tag syntax (fixed, same code block)
- #22101 — patterns containing escape sequences / character classes produce 4 consecutive
  backslashes instead of 1 (open, different symptom of the same "pattern isn't properly
  re-escaped for Go" root issue)

##### Description

When a `string` property's `pattern` constraint contains a JSON `\u00XX`-style escape for a
C0/C1 control code point (e.g. to explicitly forbid control characters in a free-text field,
a common and legitimate validation use case), the Go client generator copies the **decoded**
pattern value directly into the generated `validate:"regexp=..."` struct tag without
re-escaping it for Go source syntax.

Go disallows a literal NUL character — and
most other control characters — anywhere in source code, including inside string and raw
(backtick) string literals, so the generated file fails to compile / fails `gofmt` with:

```
illegal character NUL
```

This is the same code path that was previously patched for two other unsafe characters:
backtick (fixed in #19358, closing #19102) and comma (fixed in #24349, closing #20079).

##### openapi-generator version

Reproduced end-to-end (actual Go codegen run + `gofmt`) against **v7.25.0**. The affected
code in `AbstractGoCodegen.java` in the latest release **v7.26.0** (2026-10-06) and on `master` as of 2026-10-14, so
this still affects the current release.


##### OpenAPI declaration file content

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: control-char-pattern-repro
  version: "1.0"
paths:
  /ping:
    get:
      operationId: ping
      responses:
        "200":
          description: ok
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/TestModel"
components:
  schemas:
    TestModel:
      type: object
      properties:
        key:
          type: string
          # NOTE: as written here, this YAML/JSON "\u0000" is the standard (and only
          # valid) way to express the NUL code point in a JSON Schema pattern string.
          # It decodes to a literal control character when the spec is parsed.
          pattern: "^[^\u0000-\u001f]+$"
```

(equivalent minimal JSON spec, for convenience:)

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.0.3",
  "info": { "title": "control-char-pattern-repro", "version": "1.0" },
  "paths": {
    "/ping": {
      "get": {
        "operationId": "ping",
        "responses": {
          "200": {
            "description": "ok",
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/TestModel" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "TestModel": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "key": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^[^\u0000-\u001f]+$"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Generation Details

```shell
openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -g go \
  --input-spec spec.json \
  --output out \
  --package-name testapi \
  --enable-post-process-file \
  --global-property apis,models,modelTests=true,modelDocs=false,apiDocs=false,supportingFiles,apiTests=false
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the command above against the spec.
2. Run `gofmt -l out/model_test_model.go` (or just try to `go build`).
3. Observe:
   ```
   out/model_test_model.go:22:82: illegal character NUL
   ```
##### Actual vs expected output

Generated struct field (actual — contains two raw, non-printable bytes: 0x00 and 0x1F,
shown below as `<NUL>`/`<US>` since they are not renderable in this markdown file):

```go
Key *string `json:"key,omitempty" validate:"regexp=^[^<NUL>-<US>]+$"`
```

Expected — the pattern's control-character escapes should be re-escaped as literal Go/regex
escape text when written into the struct tag, e.g.:

```go
Key *string `json:"key,omitempty" validate:"regexp=^[^\x00-\x1f]+$"`
```

(Go's own `regexp` package correctly understands `\x00`-style hex escapes inside the pattern
text, so this would both compile and preserve the original validation semantics.)

- #22101 — patterns containing escape sequences / character classes produce 4 consecutive
  backslashes instead of 1 (open, different symptom of the same "pattern isn't properly
  re-escaped for Go" root issue)

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?

##### Description

With the C# `generichost` library, serializing a model whose **optional** (not `required`) property is an **inline string enum** throws when that property is not set:

```
System.InvalidOperationException: Nullable object must have a value.
   at System.Nullable`1.get_Value()
   at Repro.Model.PetJsonConverter.WriteProperties(...) in .../Model/Pet.cs:line 266
   at Repro.Model.PetJsonConverter.Write(...)
```

The generated `WriteProperties` writes the enum unconditionally, without the `Option.IsSet` guard that every other optional property gets:

```csharp
writer.WriteString("name", pet.Name);

var statusRawValue = Pet.StatusEnumToJsonValue(pet.StatusOption.Value!.Value);   // throws when status is unset
writer.WriteString("status", statusRawValue);
```

This makes it impossible to round-trip a response that omits the field, or to send a request body that leaves it out. Any schema with an optional inline enum is affected.

Expected: an unset optional enum is skipped, as it already is for optional strings, numbers, dates and numeric enums:

```csharp
if (pet.StatusOption.IsSet)
{
    var statusRawValue = Pet.StatusEnumToJsonValue(pet.StatusOption.Value!.Value);
    writer.WriteString("status", statusRawValue);
}
```

##### openapi-generator version

7.26.0 (latest release). I did not build master, but the template branch involved is unchanged on master (see "Suggest a fix").

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: optional inline enum repro
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /pets:
    post:
      operationId: addPet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      responses:
        '204':
          description: created
components:
  schemas:
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [available, sold]
```

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli-7.26.0.jar generate -i repro.yaml -g csharp -o out \
  --additional-properties=targetFramework=net8.0,packageName=Repro,library=generichost,nullableReferenceTypes=true
```

The same code is generated with `nullableReferenceTypes=false` (`StatusOption.Value.Value

using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
using Repro.Model;

var host = Host.CreateDefaultBuilder()

var opts = host.Services.GetRequiredService<Repro.Client.JsonSerializerOptionsProvider>()

var pet = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Pet>("{\"name\":\"Rex\"}", opts)!;   // optional "st
Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(pet, opts));                  // throws

- #24933 (error message on serialization)

`WriteProperty` partial, so it never gets the `{{^required}}if (...Option.IsSet){{/requir branch right above does use it. Wrapping the branch fixes it, for both its nullable and
non-nullable sub-branches:

```diff

             {{#isInnerEnum}}
+            {{^required}}
+            if ({{#lambda.camelcase_sanitize_param}}{{classname}}{{/lambda.camelcase_sanIsSet)
+            {
+            {{/required}}
             {{#isNullable}}
             ...
             {{/isNullable}}
             {{^isNullable}}
             ...
             {{/isNullable}}
+            {{^required}}
+            }
+            {{/required}}
             {{/isInnerEnum}}
```

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
