<!--
Please follow the issue template below for bug reports.
Also please indicate in the issue title which language/library is concerned. E.g.:  [BUG][JAVA] Bug generating foo with bar 
-->

##### Description

<!-- describe what is the question, suggestion or issue and why this is a problem for you. -->

This issue was introduced in v7.15.0 where the testify dependency was accidentally added within the `{{#hasOAuthMethods}}` condition:
https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/commit/b7fb3b210784dc5317507378a6106ad4937e663f#diff-ae8673b95d3b1db3fe17ca2fe0140cc0a679a69904257f17fdbe7a0595b75fd8R7

As a result, specs that don't require the oauth2 dependency don't get testify either. The result is that `go test ./...` fails out of the box.

Separately, when a spec _does_ use oath, the testify dependency is added to `go.mod` but not to `go.sum`. As a result, `go test ./...` still fails out of the box, but with a slightly different error.

##### openapi-generator version

<!-- which version of openapi-generator are you using, is it a regression? -->
This is still present on `master` today:
https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/master/modules/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/go/go.mod.mustache#L6-L9

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```sh
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/local" openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:v7.26.0 generate \
    -i https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/refs/heads/master/modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0/ping.yaml \
    -g go \
    -o /local/ping-test

cd ping-test
go test ./...
# github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID/test
test/api_default_test.go:14:2: no required module provides package github.com/stretchr/testify/assert; to add it:
	go get github.com/stretchr/testify/assert
FAIL	github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID/test [setup failed]
?   	github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID	[no test files]
FAIL
```

Petstore example (oauth):
```sh
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/local" openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:v7.26.0 generate \
    -i https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openapitools/openapi-generator/master/modules/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/3_0/petstore.yaml \
    -g go \
    -o /local/petstore-test

cd petstore-test
go test ./...
go: github.com/stretchr/testify@v1.10.0: missing go.sum entry for go.mod file; to add it:
	go mod download github.com/stretchr/testify
```


##### Steps to reproduce

See Generation Details above

##### Related issues/PRs

<!-- has a similar issue/PR been reported/opened before? Please do a search in https://github.com/openapitools/openapi-generator/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue%20 -->
I could not find any other issues/PRs that mention this.

##### Suggest a fix

<!-- if you can't fix the bug yourself, perhaps you can point to what might be
  causing the problem (line of code or commit), or simply make a suggestion -->
The fix for `go.mod` should be to simply update the mustache template and move the testify requirement out of the condition. One or more tests will likely need to be updated to reflect this.

For `go.sum`, the dependency is missing entirely.

For reference, running `go mod tidy` on the ping test example results in the following for me:
`go.mod`:
```
module github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID

go 1.23

require github.com/stretchr/testify v1.12.1

require go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5 // indirect
```
`go.sum`:
```
github.com/stretchr/testify v1.12.1 h1:EuwCh5fleGS7H32xRwO3wRGT7DxrDhLAT6FF8MpWDWE=
github.com/stretchr/testify v1.12.1/go.mod h1:MDEgiDPPsNp5cuIrHPPCyornHKgEVbtFUmoNlxoYthg=
go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5 h1:N6y/pJk8buWs9NY5ERU2HSMfm+IuD/OtfdAnq6kESPw=
go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5/go.mod h1:HVTZu1O7/Vkt2N+BFy8Zza+lnLsABggaTM2ZpNIGuKg=
```

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

For a `default` response, rust-axum generates a response variant with no status. The handler then calls `Response::builder().status(0)`. `0` is not a valid status code, so the builder goes into an error state:

- if the default response has a body, the next `response.headers_mut().unwrap()` (used to set `Content-Type`) panics with ``called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value``, and the connection is dropped;
- if it has no body, `response.body(..)` fails and the client gets a 500.

So an implementation has no way to return a `default` response. That includes the petstore `user` operations, whose only response is `default: successful operation`.

Expected: the implementation chooses the status code of a `default` response (this is what `default` means in OpenAPI: "any status not listed").

##### openapi-generator version

master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, 30f13393). Not a regression as far as I can tell.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: "3.0.4"
info:
  title: test
  version: "0.0.1"
paths:
  "/pets/{petId}":
    get:
      operationId: getPet
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pet
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"
        default:
          description: Unexpected error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
components:
  schemas:
    Pet:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, format: int64}
        name: {type: string}
    Error:
      type: object
      required: [code, message]
      properties:
        code: {type: integer, format: int32}
        message: {type: string}
```

##### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust-axum -i spec.yaml -o out
```

Generated (`src/apis/default.rs`, `src/server/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub enum GetPetResponse {
    Status200_ThePet(models::Pet),
    Status0_UnexpectedError(models::Error),
}

apis::default::GetPetResponse::Status0_UnexpectedError(body) => {
    let mut response = Response::builder();
    let mut response = response.status(0);
    {
        let mut response_headers = response.headers_mut().unwrap(); // panics
        ...
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the spec above with `-g rust-axum`.
2. Implement `get_pet` to return `GetPetResponse::Status0_UnexpectedError(..)`.
3. Call `GET /pets/1`: the handler panics (``called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value``). With a body-less `default` response the client gets a 500 instead.

##### Related issues/PRs

None found. rust-server has the same problem (`StatusCode::from_u16(0).expect(..)` in `server-operation-handler.mustache`).

##### Suggest a fix

Have the `default` variant carry a `u16` status chosen by the implementation, e.g. `Status0_UnexpectedError(u16, models::Error)`, or a `status` field when the variant is a struct because of headers. Validate it with `StatusCode::from_u16` (500 if invalid) and use it instead of `0`.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

The `rust` client (`reqwest` and `reqwest-trait` libraries) generates a `#[serde(untagged)]` `{Op}Error` enum with one `StatusXXX` variant per error response. It fills `ResponseContent::entity` with `serde_json::from_str(&content).ok()`, which ignores the HTTP status. When several error responses share a schema, serde takes the first variant whose shape matches, so the variant doesn't reflect the status that came back.

With the spec below, a `409` response with a `Problem` body ends up as `CreatePetError::Status400(..)`. A `404` (declared without a body) gives `entity: None`. With `supportMultipleResponses=true` the same happens to `{Op}Success`: a `201` with a `Pet` body is reported as `CreatePetSuccess::Status200(..)`.

Expected: the variant matches the response status (`Status409`, `Status404()`, `Status201`). An undeclared status maps to `DefaultResponse` if declared, otherwise `UnknownValue`.

##### openapi-generator version

master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, 30f13393). This is long-standing behavior, not a regression.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: response variant by status
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /pets:
    post:
      operationId: createPet
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: existing pet
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
        '201':
          description: created pet
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
        '400':
          description: bad request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
        '404':
          description: not found
        '409':
          description: conflict
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'
components:
  schemas:
    Pet:
      type: object
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          type: string
```

##### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust --library reqwest -i spec.yaml -o out \
  --additional-properties supportMultipleResponses=true,supportAsync=false
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the client as above.
2. Call `create_pet` against a server that returns `409` with `{"message":"conflict"}`.
3. `Error::ResponseError(r)` has `r.status == 409` but `r.entity == Some(CreatePetError::Status400(..))`.
4. A `201` with `{"name":"a"}` gives `entity == Some(CreatePetSuccess::Status200(..))`. A `404` gives `entity == None`.

##### Related issues/PRs

#10977 (asks to choose the variant by status code instead of `#[serde(untagged)]`), #22080

##### Suggest a fix

In `rust/reqwest/api.mustache` and `rust/reqwest-trait/api.mustache`, match on `status.as_u16()` and deserialize the body into that status's variant. Range codes (`4XX`) become `400..=499`, `default` becomes `_`, and bodyless variants become `Some(StatusXXX())`. If that fails, fall back to `UnknownValue`. The enums can stay as they are.

##### Description

The OpenAPI normalizer rule `SIMPLIFY_ANYOF_STRING_AND_ENUM_STRING` simplifies an "open enum" (`anyOf: [{type: string}, {type: string, enum: [...]}]`) into the enum schema. This works for 3.0 specs, but the rule does nothing for 3.1 specs: the `anyOf` is left as is.

The cause is in `OpenAPINormalizer#processSimplifyAnyOfStringAndEnumString`, which checks `s0 instanceof StringSchema && s1 instanceof StringSchema`. In 3.1 the parser creates `JsonSchema` instances instead of `StringSchema`, so the check never matches.

##### openapi-generator version

master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, 30f13393). Not a regression; the rule never supported 3.1.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  version: 1.0.0
  title: Example
  license:
    name: MIT
    identifier: MIT
paths:
  /pet:
    get:
      operationId: getPet
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PetStatus'
components:
  schemas:
    PetStatus:
      anyOf:
        - type: string
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/PetStatusEnum'
    PetStatusEnum:
      type: string
      enum:
        - available
        - sold
```

##### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust -i spec.yaml -o out --openapi-normalizer SIMPLIFY_ANYOF_STRING_AND_ENUM_STRING=true
```

Any generator shows the problem, because it comes from the normalizer.

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the spec above as `spec.yaml`.
2. Generate with `--openapi-normalizer SIMPLIFY_ANYOF_STRING_AND_ENUM_STRING=true`.
3. `PetStatus` is still treated as an `anyOf` composed schema. With `openapi: 3.0.3` (and without `info.license.identifier`), the same spec is simplified to the `available`/`sold` enum.

##### Related issues/PRs

- #14463 (added the rule)
- #15149 (improved the rule)

##### Suggest a fix

Check the schema type instead of the Java class: for `JsonSchema`, accept a schema whose `types` is exactly `["string"]`. Keep the `instanceof StringSchema` check for 3.0 so 3.0 behavior does not change.

body_text:
#### Description

With `enumUnknownDefaultCase=true` the `rust` client generator adds an `UnknownDefaultOpenApi` variant to every enum, but the variant has no `#[serde(other)]`. So serde only matches the literal string `"unknown_default_open_api"` (or the integer `11184809`). Any other value outside the spec still fails to deserialize, which defeats the purpose of the option:

```
Error("unknown variant `bird`, expected one of `cat`, `dog`, `unknown_default_open_api`", line: 1, column: 14)
```

Generated code today:

```rust
pub enum PetKind {
    #[serde(rename = "cat")]
    Cat,
    #[serde(rename = "dog")]
    Dog,
    #[serde(rename = "unknown_default_open_api")]
    UnknownDefaultOpenApi,
}
```

The same applies to inline property enums and to integer enums (`Deserialize_repr`).

#### openapi-generator version

master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, 30f13393). Not a regression.

#### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Enum unknown default case
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      operationId: listPets
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
components:
  schemas:
    Pet:
      type: object
      required:
        - kind
      properties:
        kind:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/PetKind'
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [available, sold]
        size:
          type: integer
          enum: [1, 2]
    PetKind:
      type: string
      enum: [cat, dog]
```

#### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust -i spec.yaml -o out \
  --additional-properties enumUnknownDefaultCase=true,packageName=petstore
```

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate with the command above.
2. `serde_json::from_str::<petstore::models::Pet>(r#"{"kind":"bird"}"#)` returns an error instead of `PetKind::UnknownDefaultOpenApi`. The same happens for `"status":"pending"` and `"size":7`.

#### Related issues/PRs

None found.

#### Suggest a fix

Add `#[serde(other)]` to the injected variant (the last entry of `enumVars` when `enumUnknownDefaultCase` is set) in `rust/model.mustache`, for both string and integer enums. `serde_repr` supports `#[serde(other)]` on `Deserialize_repr` enums too. Serialization stays as it is: the variant still serializes as `"unknown_default_open_api"` / `11184809`.

body_text:
##### Description

When an operation declares a range response code (`4XX`, `5XX`, ...), the rust-axum server generator emits code that does not compile. For range responses, `server-operation.mustache` renders

```rust
response.status::<u16>(body.code.parse().unwrap());  // 4XX
```

which assumes the response body has a `code` field (`error[E0609]: no field 'code' on type 'models::Error'`), fails when the response has no body (`error[E0425]: cannot find value 'body' in this scope`), and drops the builder returned by `status()` (`error[E0382]` once the other errors are worked around). The generated response enum also has no way for the implementation to choose the concrete status within the range.

##### openapi-generator version

master (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, commit 30f13393)

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Range responses
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /pets/{petId}:
    get:
      operationId: getPet
      parameters:
        - name: petId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
            format: int64
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The pet
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Pet"
        "4XX":
          description: Client error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
        "5XX":
          description: Server error
components:
  schemas:
    Pet:
      type: object
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
    Error:
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          type: string
```

##### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust-axum -i spec.yaml -o out
```

##### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the server with the spec above.
2. Run `cargo check` in `out`.
3. Compilation fails with E0609 (`no field 'code' on type 'models::Error'`) for the `4XX` arm and E0425 (`cannot find value 'body'`) for the `5XX` arm.

##### Related issues/PRs

None found.

##### Suggest a fix

Have range responses carry the status code: generate them as struct variants with a `status: u16` field (plus `body` and headers as usual), e.g. `Status4XX_ClientError { status: u16, body: models::Error }`. The server then sets `response.status(status)`, so the implementation picks the concrete code within the range.

body_text:
#### Description

When a model holds itself directly (not inside an array or map), rust-axum generates a type that does not compile. Each of these cases triggers it:

- a self reference (`parent: Node`)
- a nullable self reference (`anyOf`/`oneOf` of `[$ref, null]` in 3.1, or `nullable: true` + `allOf` in 3.0)
- a cycle through another model (`Employee.department -> Department.head -> Employee`)
- a cycle through a `oneOf` enum (`Circle.inner -> Shape`, where `Shape` is `oneOf [Circle, Square]`)

The build fails with:

```
error[E0072]: recursive type `Node` has infinite size
error[E0072]: recursive type `Employee` has infinite size
```

The generated fields (`Option<models::Node>`, `Nullable<models::Employee>`, `Option<Nullable<models::Employee>>`) have no indirection.

The rust (reqwest) client boxes model fields (unless `avoidBoxedModels` is set), so the same spec compiles there.

#### openapi-generator version

master (7.x snapshot, 30f13393)

#### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Recursive models
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /nodes:
    get:
      operationId: getNode
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Node'
components:
  schemas:
    Node:
      type: object
      required: [name]
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
        parent:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Node'
    Employee:
      type: object
      required: [name, manager]
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
        manager:
          anyOf:
            - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Employee'
            - type: 'null'
        department:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Department'
    Department:
      type: object
      properties:
        head:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Employee'
```

#### Generation Details

```
java -jar openapi-generator-cli.jar generate -g rust-axum -i spec.yaml -o out
```

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate with the command above.
2. `cd out && cargo check`
3. The build fails with E0072 for `Node` and `Employee`.

#### Related issues/PRs

#5950 (the same problem in rust-server)

#### Suggest a fix

Wrap a model field in `Box<...>` when its model can lead back to the field's own model, either directly or through other models' fields or oneOf/anyOf variants. Fields inside `Vec`/`HashMap` already have indirection and can stay as they are. Only boxing the recursive fields keeps the generated API unchanged for non-recursive models.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you tested with the latest master to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

With the `rust` client generator and `useChrono=true` (the default), `format: date-time` parameters are typed `chrono::DateTime<chrono::FixedOffset>`. Path, query and header params of that type are turned into strings with `Display` (`.to_string()` / `format!`), and chrono's `Display` is not RFC 3339:

```
GET /orders/2026-01-02%2003:04:05%20+00:00?createdAfter=2026-01-02+03%3A04%3A05+%2B00%3A00
x-request-time: 2026-01-02 03:04:05 +00:00
```

# [Python] Add native lazy import support for Python 3.15

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

OpenAPI Generator can generate Python clients with hundreds or even thousands of Pydantic models.

Currently, many of these models are imported during initialization, even when they are never used by the application.

This can lead to unnecessary memory consumption and slower startup times, especially for large API clients.

OpenAPI Generator already provides a lazy import mechanism. However, this implementation does not use Python's native lazy imports, which were recently introduced in Python 3.15 through [PEP 810](https://peps.python.org/pep-0810/) 
## Describe the solution you'd like

Add an optional configuration, such as `lazyNativeImport`, to enable native lazy imports in generated Python clients.

When enabled, the generator should:

- Generate native `lazy import` and `lazy from ... import` statements where appropriate.
- Defer loading unused modules and Pydantic models until they are needed.
- Require Python 3.15 or later.
- Keep the existing import behavior by default to maintain backward compatibility.
- Document the benefits and trade-offs of enabling native lazy imports.

**Backward compatibility**

The existing lazy import implementation should remain available for older Python versions.

Both implementations should coexist until Python 3.14 reaches End of Life (EOL), ensuring that users running earlier Python versions can continue using the current lazy import mechanism.

Once Python 3.14 reaches EOL, we can consider removing the legacy implementation and using native lazy imports instead.

Additionally, enabling Pydantic's `defer_build=True` can provide further startup memory improvements by postponing model validator and serializer construction.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Existing lazy import implementation:** Continue using the current OpenAPI Generator lazy import mechanism, which supports older Python versions but does not take advantage of Python 3.15's native lazy imports.
- **Manual native lazy imports:** Modify the generated client after generation to use Python 3.15's native lazy imports. This works but requires maintaining custom changes whenever the client is regenerated.
- **Pydantic `defer_build=True`:** Helps reduce initialization overhead but does not prevent unused model modules from being imported.

## Additional context

I created a proof of concept using Python 3.15's native lazy imports with an OpenAPI-generated client.

The initial results showed a significant reduction in memory consumption.

**References:**

- [PEP 810 – Explicit lazy imports](https://peps.python.org/pep-0810/)
- [What's New in Python 3.15](https://docs.python.org/3.15/whatsnew/3.15.html)
- [Pydantic – defer_build](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/config/#pydantic.config.ConfigDict.defer_build)
- [Python versions and EOL schedule](https://devguide.python.org/versions/)

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [ ] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [ ] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?

##### Description

With `useBeanValidation` (default for `kotlin-spring`), `beanValidation.mustache` puts `@field:Valid` on container properties (`List`, `Set`, `Map`) and on free-form `kotlin.Any` properties.

Hibernate Validator 9.1 (shipped with Spring Boot 4.1) deprecated container-level `@Valid` and logs a warning while building bean metadata:

```
WARN org.hibernate.validator.internal.metadata.aggregated.CascadingMetaDataBuilder - HV000271: Using `@Valid` on a container (java.util.List) is deprecated. You should apply the annotation on the type argument(s). Affected element: items
WARN org.hibernate.validator.internal.metadata.aggregated.CascadingMetaDataBuilder - HV000272: Using `@Valid` on a container is deprecated. You should apply the annotation on the type argument(s). (java.lang.Object) can potentially be a container at runtime. Affected element: customInfo
```

Because the bean metadata cache in Hibernate Validator uses soft references, the warnings are not logged only once at startup - they are repeated each time the metadata of a rarely used model is evicted and rebuilt, which produces a steady stream of warnings in production logs.

The same problem was fixed for the Java generators in #24176 (released in 7.26.0, issue #23614) by moving `@Valid` to the type argument. The `kotlin-spring` templates were not touched. An attempt for Kotlin (#24027 / #24029) only removed `@field:Valid` from `Map` properties and was closed, because that silently drops cascading validation of the values.

**Actual output**

```kotlin
data class Pet(
    @field:Valid
    @get:JsonProperty("items") val items: kotlin.collections.List<Item>? = null,

    @field:Valid
    @get:JsonProperty("itemsByKey") val itemsByKey: kotlin.collections.Map<kotlin.String, Item>? = null,
```

```kotlin
    @get:JsonProperty("itemsByKey") val itemsByKey: kotlin.collections.Map<kotlin.String, @Valid Item>? = null,
```

```kotlin
  configOptions.put("useSpringBoot3", "true")
```

1. Generate the models from the spec above with `kotlin-spring`.
2. Validate a `Pet` instance with Hibernate Validator 9.1 (e.g. `Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory().validator.validate(Pet(items = listOf(Item(name = ""))))`).

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The `python-pydantic-v1` generator still contains outdated Python version requirements and CI configurations.

Some templates reference Python 3.7 or 3.8 as minimum versions, while CI configurations include older Python releases.

This creates inconsistencies between package metadata and testing configurations and increases the maintenance burden of supporting older Python versions.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I propose modernizing the Python version requirements and CI configurations for the `python-pydantic-v1` generator.

The changes would include:

- **Minimum Python version:** Update `pyproject.mustache` and `setup.mustache` to require Python 3.11 or newer.
- **GitHub Actions:** Update the Python test matrix to cover versions 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
- **GitLab CI:** Update the test jobs to use Python 3.11 through 3.14.
- **Travis CI:** Align the Python versions with the other CI configurations.
- **Generated samples:** Regenerate the affected samples to reflect the updated templates.

The goal is to simplify maintenance, remove outdated configurations, and keep the generator aligned with more recent Python versions.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

An alternative would be to retain support for older Python versions and update only the CI configurations.

However, this would preserve the additional maintenance burden and inconsistencies between the supported versions and the test environments.

## Additional context

The proposed changes are limited to the `python-pydantic-v1` generator templates and their generated samples.

The main files involved are:

- `python-pydantic-v1/github-workflow.mustache`
- `python-pydantic-v1/gitlab-ci.mustache`
- `python-pydantic-v1/pyproject.mustache`
- `python-pydantic-v1/setup.mustache`
- `python-pydantic-v1/travis.mustache`

I have already prepared a local implementation of these changes.

Since increasing the minimum supported Python version is a breaking change for users running older versions, I would like to discuss whether this direction is acceptable before submitting a pull request.

#### Bug Report Checklist

- [x] Have you provided a full/minimal spec to reproduce the issue?
- [x] Have you validated the input using an OpenAPI validator?
- [x] Have you [tested with the latest master](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/wiki/FAQ#how-to-test-with-the-latest-master-of-openapi-generator) to confirm the issue still exists?
- [x] Have you searched for related issues/PRs?
- [x] What's the actual output vs expected output?
- [ ] [Optional] Sponsorship to speed up the bug fix or feature request ([example](https://redirect.github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/issues/6178))

##### Description

When an array's `items` (or a parameter's schema) is an `allOf` with a single `$ref`, the PHP generators emit the referenced model's fully qualified name with every namespace separator stripped:

```php
'errors_wrapped' => '\AcmeClientModelError[]',   // generated
'errors_plain'   => '\Acme\Client\Model\Error[]', // same model, plain $ref
```

and for a query parameter:

```php
?\AcmeClientModelSortDir $sort = null,
```

`\AcmeClientModelError` is not a class, so `ObjectSerializer::deserialize()` fails on any response that carries such an array, and the API method signature references a type that cannot be autoloaded.

The `allOf: [ $ref ]` wrapper is the standard way to attach a `description`, `readOnly` or `nullable` to a `$ref`, so real-world specs hit this constantly (one large public carrier API spec we generate from has over 300 such references).

A single-member `allOf` directly on a *property* is fine, because `DefaultCodegen.fromProperty()` unwraps it before resolving the type. Array items and parameters do not go through that unwrapping.

##### openapi-generator version

7.26.0, and reproduced on current `master` (7.27.0-SNAPSHOT, built locally). Both `php` and `php-nextgen` are affected because the logic lives in `AbstractPhpCodegen`. Not a regression as far as I can tell; the override responsible has been there for a long time.

##### OpenAPI declaration file content or url

Validated with `openapi-generator-cli validate` (no errors or warnings).

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: allOf item repro
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /things:
    get:
      operationId: listThings
      parameters:
        - name: sort
          in: query
          schema:
            allOf:
              - $ref: '#/components/schemas/sort_dir'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: ok
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/thing_list'
components:
  schemas:
    sort_dir:
```

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

`jaxrs-spec` is hardcoded to Jackson 2.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Support Jackson 3.

Bonus, though not critical, for doing it via `useJackson3` (e.g. `JavaJAXRSSpecServerCodegen.useJackson3` ), just to remain similar to the other libraries that already support this.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Adding custom imports for the Jackson types is likely to work (until it doesn't).
It feels like a pretty fragile alternative, though.

Currently on Windows 10, clicking `openrefine.exe` will cause extra security warnings for Microsoft Defender SmartScreen.

### Proposed solution
I think only 1 option exists:

1. Since OpenRefine is downloaded from GitHub website and not through our own OpenRefine website the SmartScreen technology considers the openrefine.exe as unsafe since it is not digitally signed and verified with Microsoft and/or doesn't come from a trusted website.

### Alternatives considered
* Bypassing SmartScreen every time to run - must click "More Info" on SmartScreen blocking dialog and then "Run Anyways"
* Bypassing SmartScreen permanently - After downloading and extracting the .zip file, right clicking on `openrefine.exe` and clicking **Unblock** to add openrefine.exe to safe list for SmartScreen so that it does not block and instead considers it safe.

### Additional context
Some non-exhaustive details I have found:
* MSIX - all packages inside get signed recursively https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/msix/package/signing-package-overview
* https://fb.smartscreen.microsoft.com/smartscreenfaq.aspx
* [Windows App Certification Kit](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/uwp/debug-test-perf/windows-app-certification-kit)
* https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/protect/forum/all/how-verifyed-publisher-status-makes-an-application/d4c81d5c-79bf-4caf-89da-5e4747b571e7

Hitting a "deduplicate" button would then remove duplicate entries (col1_selected, ..., colM_selected)

Expression Editor preview is very slow in updating when there are many records/elements (objects?) in an array that need to be shown or previewed.

When there is a large array (Records, etc.) that is shown in Expression Editor preview, then for each element/subelement, there are multiple style changes that seem to occur, and for each one, the layout is being updated, over and over, in rapid succession.  We are effectively looping and updating the DOM with style changes multiple times and writing each one out... rather than just reading the updated values and then finally writing them out.

Details of how to improve this:
https://web.dev/articles/avoid-large-complex-layouts-and-layout-thrashing?utm_source=devtools#avoid-forced-synchronous-layouts

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start up Edge Dev Tools (or similar in another browser) to record a performance profile
2. Paste into an OpenRefine grid cell via `edit` any very large amount of HTML record text (see attached OpenRefine project "NPM-Packages" where Column 1 was/can be used)
3. Edit Column -> Add column based on... with just `value` , as long as there's a lot of HTML, or you can also do a `value.parseHtml().select("ol > li").join("|||")`
4. After the preview shows, Stop the profiling
5. Notice the performance profile results

### Current Results
Load this Profile in Edge Dev Tools, if you want to see and compare to my own profile run:
[Trace-20240107T111209.zip](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/files/13852105/Trace-20240107T111209.zip)


### Expected Behavior
Iterating and reading all the style updates first, then a single final layout to render and update the DOM?

### Screenshots
![image](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/assets/986438/271e94a1-8eab-45a0-9d81-d98cc30cd863)


### Versions<!--  (please complete the following information)-->
 - Operating System: Windows 11
 - Browser Version: Edge Version 121.0.2277.4 (Official build) stable app, beta channel (64-bit)
 - JRE or JDK Version: OpenJDK 21
 - OpenRefine: 3.7.7

### Datasets
[NPM-Packages.openrefine.tar.gz](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/files/13852104/NPM-Packages.openrefine.tar.gz)


### Additional context
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. -->

When there is a large array (Records, etc.) that is shown in Expression Editor preview, then for each element/subelement, there are multiple style changes that seem to occur, and for each one, the layout is being updated, over and over, in rapid succession.  We are effectively looping and updating the DOM with style changes multiple times and writing each one out... rather than just reading the updated values and then finally writing them out.

Details of how to improve this:
https://web.dev/articles/avoid-large-complex-layouts-and-layout-thrashing?utm_source=devtools#avoid-forced-synchronous-layouts

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start up Edge Dev Tools (or similar in another browser) to record a performance profile
2. Paste into an OpenRefine grid cell via `edit` any very large amount of HTML record text (see attached OpenRefine project "NPM-Packages" where Column 1 was/can be used)
3. Edit Column -> Add column based on... with just `value` , as long as there's a lot of HTML, or you can also do a `value.parseHtml().select("ol > li").join("|||")`

[Trace-20240107T111209.zip](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/files/13852105/Trace-20240107T111209.zip)


### Expected Behavior
Iterating and reading all the style updates first, then a single final layout to render and update the DOM?

body_text: OpenRefine has connectors for SQLLite, MariaDB, etc., but no connector yet for DuckDB, a highly popular database architecture, especially in the R community. ### Proposed solution Develop new connector logic. Phase one is narrowly scoped to read only operations against a DuckDB database, with no write functionality. A pull request for this is already submitted and will be linked back to this issue. If phase one is successful, then the contributor would plan to submit a phase two pull request with the supplemental functionality needed to write to DuckDB databases from OpenRefine. ### Alternatives considered There is not yet any OpenRefine connector to DuckDB. Workarounds are possible (e.g., tsv export and import), but add unnecessary extra steps. ### Additional context Already built, tested, and working.

body_text: ### Use case or need Wikidata has [a new mass-editing policy](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Mass-editing_policy). It would be unfortunate if OpenRefine users got themselves in trouble out of ignorance of its existence. ### What would improve? We should provide a link to the policy in relevant places. ### Proposed solution (optional) I guess that message `perform-wikibase-edits/review-your-edits ` in [extensions/wikibase/module/scripts/dialogs/perform-edits-dialog.js](https://github.com/OpenRefine/OpenRefine/blob/815f46abcb51d21cd96197b749e023462487e47c/extensions/wikibase/module/scripts/dialogs/perform-edits-dialog.js#L94) is the relevant message. The current English wording is: > "You are about to upload $1 edits to $3. Please check them carefully. Large edit batches should be submitted for bot review first." A new wording could be: > "You are about to upload $1 edits to $3. Please check them carefully. Large edit batches should be submitted for bot review first and all edits should comply with the mass-editing policy."

body_text: This issue is only for Safari (MacOs 26.7.1), and only started after a recent update to version 27.0 (of Safari). I know we officially don't support Safari but I was happily using it until a Safari update had a peculiar effect on my OR tables, so I thought someone might be interested in investigating. After opening my project and then setting a simple text facet on any column, my All column (i.e. the first column which is not resizable) becomes absurdly wide (sometimes wider than the width of my window) even though there's practically nothing in it but a small index number and flags and stars. It does seem to be content-dependent because if I try this with a simple small project, I don't get the issue. That is to say that I can't tell you how to reproduce the issue without giving you one of my project files but these are confidential. They are pretty ordinary tables with a few thousand rows and a few dozen columns - perhaps the extenuating factor is that there are cells with strings of about 100 characters long which seem to be determining the height of the rows. And as a side issue, in case anyone is looking into Safari support, the column resizing functionality is generally quite broken in Safari (which has been the case ever since the resizing functionality was added).

### Community note

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.


### OpenTofu Version

```shell
$ tofu version
OpenTofu v1.12.6
on linux_amd64
```

### The problem in your OpenTofu project

Unable to control the recreation of resources/modules such that one instance of an active/standby cluster is completely recreated before the other ensuring that at least one instance remains online throughout the process.

### Attempted Solutions

The closest it appears you can get today is the use of depends_on.  However, during the above scenario, both will be destroyed in reverse order of dependency and then recreated in order of dependency.  You have a time when both machines are gone.


### Proposal

Propose that a lifecycle option called `sequential_group` or similar be added that will cause resources or modules that are members of the same group to be applied completely sequentially and cause a failure if one fails without proceeding on with other members in the group.

The use case for this is instances where you have, for example, an active/standby pair of machines deployed from a common image.  A new image becomes available and both must be recreated.  You want one to be completely recreated before the other.

This should also be applicable to modules, whereby all operations for resources within a module are completed before another module of the same group.  For simplicity, it may be that a `sequential_group` can only contain modules OR resources.   Resources within modules may be parallelized in the usual way.


### Workarounds and Alternatives

Tried multiple incarnations of depends_on.  The only way I can see that doesnt involve `-target` is to maintain an active stack and standby stack.

Unable to control the recreation of resources/modules such that one instance of an active/standby cluster is completely recreated before the other ensuring that at least one instance remains online throughout the process.

### Attempted Solutions

The closest it appears you can get today is the use of depends_on.  However, during the above scenario, both will be destroyed in reverse order of dependency and then recreated in order of dependency.  You have a time when both machines are gone.


### Proposal

Propose that a lifecycle option called `sequential_group` or similar be added that will cause resources or modules that are members of the same group to be applied completely sequentially and cause a failure if one fails without proceeding on with other members in the group.

For simplicity, it may be that a `sequential_group` can only contain modules OR resources.   Resources within modules may be parallelized in the usual way.


### Workarounds and Alternatives

Tried multiple incarnations of depends_on.  The only way I can see that doesnt involve `-target` is to maintain an active stack and standby stack.

### Community note

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.

### OpenTofu Version

```shell
OpenTofu v1.12.6
OpenTofu v1.13.0-beta1
```

Both affected. Terraform 1.8.3 and 1.16.2 accept the same configuration.

### OpenTofu Configuration Files

`main.tf`:

```hcl
variable "input" {
  type = string
}

output "out" {
  value = var.input
}
```

`main.tftest.hcl`:

```hcl
variables {
  helper = "hello"
}

run "check" {
  command = plan

  variables {
    input = var.helper
  }

  assert {
    condition     = output.out == "hello"
    error_message = "expected hello"
  }
}
```

Note that `helper` is declared only in the test file's top-level `variables` block — it is
deliberately not a variable of the module under test.

### Debug Output

```
main.tftest.hcl... fail
  run "check"... fail

Error: No value for required variable

  on main.tf line 1:
   1: variable "input" {

The root module input variable "input" is not set, and has no default value.

Error: Unsupported attribute

  on main.tftest.hcl line 9, in run "check":
   9:     input = var.helper
    ├────────────────
    │ var is object with no attributes

This object does not have an attribute named "helper".

Failure! 0 passed, 1 failed.
```

### Expected Behavior

`var.helper` inside a `run` block's `variables` block resolves to the value defined in the
test file's top-level `variables` block, so the module receives `input = "hello"` and the test
passes. This is what Terraform does — `terraform test` reports `Success! 1 passed, 0 failed.`
on 1.8.3 and on 1.16.2.

### Actual Behavior

`var` is an object with no attributes inside the `run` block's `variables` block, so the
reference fails and the module variable ends up unset.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `tofu init`
2. `tofu test`

### Additional Context

This pattern is useful for expressing a value once and reusing it in both the inputs of a run
block and its assertions, which is how we hit it: a shared module's test file defines a set of
expected backoff/retry values at file level and references them from several `run` blocks.

#1213 added support for `var.` references *in* the top-level `variables` block (resolving to
module input values supplied via `tfvars`/`TF_VAR_`). This report is the other direction:
referencing a top-level test variable *from* a `run` block. I could not find an existing issue
covering it.

### References

- #1213 — related, but about `var.` inside the top-level `variables` block

### Workaround

Verified working on OpenTofu 1.12.6 and 1.13.0-beta1, and still passing on Terraform 1.8.3 and
1.16.2, so the reshaped file stays portable:

- Inline the value at each use site and delete the top-level `variables` block, or
- if the value is worth defining once, declare it as a variable *of the module under test* with
  a default and reference `var.<name>` — module variables resolve correctly in both tools.

The second option keeps the "define once" property but changes the module's public surface,
which is unattractive for a shared module. Neither is a reason not to fix the reference, but
both unblock today.

### Community note

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.

### OpenTofu Version

```shell
OpenTofu v1.12.6
OpenTofu v1.13.0-beta1
```

Both affected. Terraform 1.8.3 and 1.16.2 accept the same configuration.

### OpenTofu Configuration Files

`main.tf`:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    local = {
      source  = "hashicorp/local"
      version = "2.5.2"
    }
  }
}

data "local_file" "example" {
  filename = "does-not-exist.txt"
}

output "content" {
  value = data.local_file.example.content
}
```

`main.tftest.hcl`:

```hcl
override_data {
  target = data.local_file.example
  values = {
    filename = "overridden.txt"
    content  = "overridden content"
  }
}

run "check" {
  command = plan

  assert {
    condition     = output.content == "overridden content"
    error_message = "expected the overridden content"
  }
}
```

### Debug Output

```
Error: Invalid mock/override field `filename`

Error: Non-computed field `filename` is not allowed to be overridden
```

### Expected Behavior

The `override_data` block replaces the data source entirely, so supplying a value for an
argument alongside the computed attributes is accepted and the run passes. Terraform reports
`Success! 1 passed, 0 failed.` on both 1.8.3 and 1.16.2.

### Actual Behavior

OpenTofu rejects the block because `filename` is an argument rather than a computed attribute,
and the whole test file fails.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `tofu init`
2. `tofu test`

### Additional Context

I am not sure whether this is a bug or a deliberate design choice — refusing to override
something the configuration already controls is defensible. Raising it because it is a
behavioural difference from Terraform that breaks otherwise-portable test files, and because
the diagnostic reads as a hard error rather than a documented restriction.

Our real case is a data source whose `name` argument is echoed back by the provider, so the
override lists it next to `id` to describe the object as a whole. Dropping the argument from
`values` is a viable workaround if the current behaviour is intended — in which case
documenting the restriction (and ideally naming the offending field as a warning rather than
failing the file) would be enough.

`override_data` type-checking was tightened in #1903 / #2220 (warning to error on type
mismatch); this is a different rule — field *kind* rather than value type. I could not find an
existing issue for it.

### References

- #2008 — earlier `override_data` problems, closed
- #1903 / #2220 — warning-to-error change for incorrect override value *types*

### Workaround

Omit the argument from `values` and let it resolve from the configuration as normal:

```hcl
override_data {
  target = data.local_file.example
  values = {
    content = "overridden content"
  }
}
```

Verified on OpenTofu 1.12.6 and 1.13.0-beta1, and still passing on Terraform 1.8.3 and 1.16.2.
`data.local_file.example.filename` still evaluates to the value in the configuration, so
nothing is lost as long as the argument is one the test already controls. That is a good sign
the current restriction is at least defensible — but the diagnostic gives no hint that dropping
the field is the intended shape.

### Community note

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.


### OpenTofu Version

```shell
OpenTofu v1.14.0-dev
on darwin_arm64
```

### The problem in your OpenTofu project

I run OpenTofu drift checks on a schedule and in CI, across a lot of workspaces. I want them to fire only when something has actually changed outside of OpenTofu, and to never be able to change anything themselves.

Detection isn't the missing piece, though it's fiddly. `tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode` already returns exit `2` only when there's drift (an unapplied config change doesn't trigger it), and `-json` emits `resource_drift`, but you have to know that exact flag combination and parse the JSON to see what actually changed. Two bigger things are the problem.

First, I can't tell a check to ignore drift I already know about, just for that run. There's always some noise, like a tag a scanner rewrites every hour or an attribute the provider keeps normalizing. My only knob today is `ignore_changes`, and it's the wrong tool for an alarm (more on that below). So I either get paged for noise or mute the whole resource and miss real drift on it.

Second, the check isn't guaranteed read-only. I'm running `plan`, which takes `-out` and is one step from something appliable. I'd be a lot more comfortable scheduling that across dozens of workspaces, or handing it to compliance, if it simply couldn't change anything.

### Attempted Solutions

For finding drift the refresh-only route is fine.

```
tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode          # 2 on drift, 0 otherwise
tofu plan -refresh-only -json | jq '[.. | select(.type? == "resource_drift")]'
```

It's the suppression part that breaks down. Take that scanner rewriting `tags["LastScanned"]` every hour, so every run lights up on it. Right now I have two options.

- Put `ignore_changes = [tags["LastScanned"]]` in the config. That quiets the alarm, but now `apply` won't reconcile that tag either, it needs a review, and it's global, not scoped to this one check.
- Filter the `-json` in `jq` and work out the exit code myself. That's a fragile script I have to babysit per resource type.

Neither lets me ignore that one tag for this check while still failing on any other drift.

### Proposal

I'd propose a `tofu drift` command. What makes it more than a wrapper around `plan -refresh-only` is a `-ignore` flag that hides expected drift from the report, and only the report.

`tofu drift -ignore=aws_s3_bucket.demo` drops a whole resource; `-ignore='aws_instance.web:tags["LastScanned"]'` drops one attribute. The address is just the normal resource instance address you already use in plan output and `-target` (count/for_each and modules work, managed resources only), and the attribute part is the same syntax as `ignore_changes`. It only affects what's printed, never state, never infra, never what a later plan or apply does. If it can't apply a rule cleanly, it shows the full drift instead, and anything it hides is still counted and labeled. It only masks what you name, so if the same resource drifted somewhere else you still see it and the check still fails. That's the one thing the refresh-only plus `jq` route can't do without a config change, and it's the part I've built.

The command itself is small.

```
tofu drift          # human-readable report
tofu drift -json    # adds a drift_summary with counts
```

A few specifics.

- It's strictly read-only. It forces refresh-only and rejects `-destroy` and `-refresh=false` (without a refresh it would report "no drift" regardless of the real state), and it can't apply or destroy under any arguments, which a `plan`-based check can't promise.
- Exit codes are `0` no drift, `1` error, `2` drift. The `2` lines up with what `plan -detailed-exitcode` already means. There's no "drift plus pending config" case to worry about, since refresh-only never looks at config changes, and if the refresh itself falls over that's just an error (`1`).
- In `-json` the only new thing is a `drift_summary` message with `changed`/`deleted`/`total`/`ignored`. `resource_drift` is the existing message, untouched.

`tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode -json` already handles detection and gives a clean exit code, so this isn't about finding drift. It's about being able to suppress expected drift per run, and having one read-only command to reach for instead of that flag combination.

On scope, in case it matters for the decision, this is a CLI-layer change with nothing touched in the core engine or the backends. I'll share the full diff when there's a PR.

Related: #28803 asked for a way to hide expected changes from the refresh report, and #30486 handled that for the plan view by only showing changes that fed into the plan. `-ignore` is a different, complementary thing: explicit, under my control, per run, aimed at a standalone check rather than tidying up a full plan.

**_I've got a working version with tests and I've run it against a real AWS provider, so I'm happy to share the branch._** But per CONTRIBUTING I wanted to sort out direction before dropping code. The real question is do you want a read-only drift command with a suppression flag at all, or would you rather the suppression just be a flag on `plan -refresh-only`? Since `-ignore` is the whole reason for the command, I'd put it in v1, though I'm happy to stage its surface (resource-level first, attribute-level as a follow-up) if you'd prefer something smaller to start. Glad to turn this into an RFC if you tag it `needs-rfc`. I've filed the same thing for Terraform at hashicorp/terraform#39172.

### Workarounds and Alternatives

The closest thing today is `tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode` plus `-json | jq`, which I covered above. It finds drift fine, it just can't suppress per run.

If a new command is the wrong shape, the obvious alternative is to hang `-ignore` (and a drift-scoped exit code) off `plan -refresh-only`, and honestly I'd be fine with that. The catch is `plan` still can't promise read-only (it takes `-out`), and its flag list is already long. A `plan -drift-only` flag has the same problem, and actually changing what `plan -detailed-exitcode` returns is off the table since it'd break everyone relying on today's `0`/`1`/`2`. Only a separate command can actually guarantee read-only.

### References

A few related Terraform issues for context, given the shared history. I'm citing them as prior art.

- hashicorp/terraform#39172 (the parallel Terraform proposal)
- hashicorp/terraform#28803 (closed, addressed by #30486): the drift-report noise problem; #30486 de-noised the plan view, `-ignore` is the per-run lever for a standalone check.
- hashicorp/terraform#35226 (open): asks that `plan` exit `0` when everything matches, showing demand for drift-scoped exit semantics.

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.


### OpenTofu Version

```shell
OpenTofu v1.14.0-dev
on darwin_arm64
```

### The problem in your OpenTofu project

I run OpenTofu drift checks on a schedule and in CI, across a lot of workspaces. I want them to fire only when something has actually changed outside of OpenTofu, and to never be able to change anything themselves.

Detection isn't the missing piece, though it's fiddly. `tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode` already returns exit `2` only when there's drift (an unapplied config change doesn't trigger it), and `-json` emits `resource_drift`, but you have to know that exact flag combination and parse the JSON to see what actually changed. Two bigger things are the problem.

First, I can't tell a check to ignore drift I already know about, just for that run. There's always some noise, like a tag a scanner rewrites every hour or an attribute the provider keeps normalizing. My only knob today is `ignore_changes`, and it's the wrong tool for an alarm (more on that below). So I either get paged for noise or mute the whole resource and miss real drift on it.

Second, the check isn't guaranteed read-only. I'm running `plan`, which takes `-out` and is one step from something appliable. I'd be a lot more comfortable scheduling that across dozens of workspaces, or handing it to compliance, if it simply couldn't change anything.

### Attempted Solutions

For finding drift the refresh-only route is fine.

```
tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode          # 2 on drift, 0 otherwise
tofu plan -refresh-only -json | jq '[.. | select(.type? == "resource_drift")]'
```

It's the suppression part that breaks down. Take that scanner rewriting `tags["LastScanned"]` every hour, so every run lights up on it. Right now I have two options.

- Put `ignore_changes = [tags["LastScanned"]]` in the config. That quiets the alarm, but now `apply` won't reconcile that tag either, it needs a review, and it's global, not scoped to this one check.
- Filter the `-json` in `jq` and work out the exit code myself. That's a fragile script I have to babysit per resource type.

Neither lets me ignore that one tag for this check while still failing on any other drift.

### Proposal

I'd propose a `tofu drift` command. What makes it more than a wrapper around `plan -refresh-only` is a `-ignore` flag that hides expected drift from the report, and only the report.

`tofu drift -ignore=aws_s3_bucket.demo` drops a whole resource; `-ignore='aws_instance.web:tags["LastScanned"]'` drops one attribute. The address is just the normal resource instance address you already use in plan output and `-target` (count/for_each and modules work, managed resources only), and the attribute part is the same syntax as `ignore_changes`. It only affects what's printed, never state, never infra, never what a later plan or apply does. If it can't apply a rule cleanly, it shows the full drift instead, and anything it hides is still counted and labeled. It only masks what you name, so if the same resource drifted somewhere else you still see it and the check still fails. That's the one thing the refresh-only plus `jq` route can't do without a config change, and it's the part I've built.

The command itself is small.

```
tofu drift          # human-readable report
tofu drift -json    # adds a drift_summary with counts
```

A few specifics.

- It's strictly read-only. It forces refresh-only and rejects `-destroy` and `-refresh=false` (without a refresh it would report "no drift" regardless of the real state), and it can't apply or destroy under any arguments, which a `plan`-based check can't promise.
- Exit codes are `0` no drift, `1` error, `2` drift. The `2` lines up with what `plan -detailed-exitcode` already means. There's no "drift plus pending config" case to worry about, since refresh-only never looks at config changes, and if the refresh itself falls over that's just an error (`1`).
- In `-json` the only new thing is a `drift_summary` message with `changed`/`deleted`/`total`/`ignored`. `resource_drift` is the existing message, untouched.

`tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode -json` already handles detection and gives a clean exit code, so this isn't about finding drift. It's about being able to suppress expected drift per run, and having one read-only command to reach for instead of that flag combination.

On scope, in case it matters for the decision, this is a CLI-layer change with nothing touched in the core engine or the backends. I'll share the full diff when there's a PR.

Related: #28803 asked for a way to hide expected changes from the refresh report, and #30486 handled that for the plan view by only showing changes that fed into the plan. `-ignore` is a different, complementary thing: explicit, under my control, per run, aimed at a standalone check rather than tidying up a full plan.

**_I've got a working version with tests and I've run it against a real AWS provider, so I'm happy to share the branch._** But per CONTRIBUTING I wanted to sort out direction before dropping code. The real question is do you want a read-only drift command with a suppression flag at all, or would you rather the suppression just be a flag on `plan -refresh-only`? Since `-ignore` is the whole reason for the command, I'd put it in v1, though I'm happy to stage its surface (resource-level first, attribute-level as a follow-up) if you'd prefer something smaller to start. Glad to turn this into an RFC if you tag it `needs-rfc`. I've filed the same thing for Terraform at hashicorp/terraform#39172.

### Workarounds and Alternatives

The closest thing today is `tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode` plus `-json | jq`, which I covered above. It finds drift fine, it just can't suppress per run.

If a new command is the wrong shape, the obvious alternative is to hang `-ignore` (and a drift-scoped exit code) off `plan -refresh-only`, and honestly I'd be fine with that. The catch is `plan` still can't promise read-only (it takes `-out`), and its flag list is already long. A `plan -drift-only` flag has the same problem, and actually changing what `plan -detailed-exitcode` returns is off the table since it'd break everyone relying on today's `0`/`1`/`2`. Only a separate command can actually guarantee read-only.

### References

A few related Terraform issues for context, given the shared history. I'm citing them as prior art.

- hashicorp/terraform#39172 (the parallel Terraform proposal)
- hashicorp/terraform#28803 (closed, addressed by #30486): the drift-report noise problem; #30486 de-noised the plan view, `-ignore` is the per-run lever for a standalone check.
- hashicorp/terraform#35226 (open): asks that `plan` exit `0` when everything matches, showing demand for drift-scoped exit semantics.

### Community note

> [!TIP]
> 👋 Hi there, OpenTofu community! The OpenTofu team prioritizes issues based on upvotes. Please make sure to upvote this issue and describe how it affects you in detail in the comments to show your support.


### OpenTofu Version

```shell
1.12.6
```

### The problem in your OpenTofu project

I would like to be able to use first class OpenTofu functionality to allow me to mimic the behavior of the Google provider's `deletion_protection`/`deletion_policy`/etc on any resource that I specify, not just ones where the provider has specifically built this protection into that specific resource type. This means that deletion protection information is stored in the state file and any plans or applies that would cause the protected resource to be deleted fail with an error saying that I'm trying to delete a resource that has deletion protection enabled and deletion protection must first be disabled before I attempt to do the deletion.

This deletion protection field must be able to reference a dynamic value such as variables and locals, it is not viable to use the historical behavior of the `prevent_destroy` lifecycle rule where it could only be hardcoded `true`/`false` even if it lives on a resource inside a module.

Note to maintainers - feel free to edit this issue.

### Attempted Solutions

See Workarounds and Alternatives section below

### Proposal

Implement state based deletion protection, similar to how the Google provider does it, so that it will generate an error if deletion protection is enabled and the plan shows a deletion of the resource because one of the following conditions is met:

- A module call is removed
- A resource block is removed
- An instance of a module call is removed (`count`/`for_each`/`enabled`)
- An instance of a resource is removed (`count`/`for_each`/`enabled`)
- An instance of a resource will be deleted and re-created

This must be able to reference a dynamic value such as variables, it is not viable to use the historical behavior of the `prevent_destroy` lifecycle rule where it could only be hardcoded `true`/`false` even if it lives on a resource inside a module.

I can see a few different options for how someone would delete or re-create a resource that is currently protected by this deletion protection:

1. Copy the current behavior of the Google provider which involves the following steps. This is the most toil (2-3 separate PRs/applies) but is the most explicit and also matches the workflow that users sometimes have to follow to disable cloud-side deletion protection.
    1. Do an apply that disabled deletion protection
    2. Make the change that results in deletion or re-creation and apply it
    3. (If necessary) Do an apply that re-enables deletion protection
2. Allow users to change deletion protection in the same apply as the action that performs the destruction.
    1. If the resource instance is being re-created, this means that you would
        1. Change the deletion protection value and make the change that triggers the re-creation in the same PR/apply
        2. Do an apply that re-enables deletion protection
    2. If the module or resource instance is being removed, do something similar to the existing `removed` block that tells OpenTofu this module or resource instance has been deliberately removed and overrides the deletion protection that is saved in the state file.
        1. Remove the module or resource instance and add the `deleted` block (or whatever you name it) in a single PR/apply
        2. Clean up the `deleted` block, same as how you can remove a `removed`, `import`, or `moved` block once they have been executed
3. Have a CLI option similar to `taint` that removes the deletion protection for just the next apply (or potentially allow the existing `taint` functionality to override the deletion protection). Given the general move away from CLI only operations, I don't love this option, but wanted to include for completeness. I don't think this would be good to do in a `.tf` file similar to how the `moved` block works since a user could easily forget to remove the block after the apply has occurred and it would be better for the user to set and feed the value through as a variable to their resource or module call where they can do variable validation rules or additional checks on their end.

### Workarounds and Alternatives

1. `prevent_destroy`, but this has significant limitations, as listed in https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/issues/4569 and doesn't actually prevent destruction when the resource or module block is removed.
2. Using provider created resource specific functionality like the Google provider has. However, this has significant limitations in that it is rarely available, has to be added per specific individual resource, adds a lot of overhead for provider maintainers, and provider maintainers have to add this functionality per individual resource instead of users being able to determine which resources they do or do not want to use it with.
3. Using OPA policies. However, this adds significant overhead and complexity to CI/CD tooling compared to a first class, native OpenTofu functionality. Additionally, these are often not evaluated as part of PR plans or local development plans, which creates a poor developer experience and longer cycle times.

### References

- https://github.com/opentofu/opentofu/issues/4569
- https://opentofu.org/docs/language/resources/behavior/#lifecycle-customizations
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/17599
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/issues/20729
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/issues/25072
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/3116
